docs/assets/STR-01.md:
# STR-01 Great Rock Spire, Large: Blueprint

> **Proposed look, from the asset description.** The numbers come from the island blueprints that use it. Where this page and a Gemini picture disagree, this page wins.

## 1. What it is
A colossal tapering natural rock spire, seven rough narrowing tiers of stacked fractured strata, a deep vertical crack down one side, the top sheared off in a jagged diagonal break, standing on a rough rock base with fallen boulders, grand and ominous. Natural dark black-brown fractured rock only, in the same rock as the ENV-01 hero: sharp angular faces, horizontal strata, long vertical cracks, grime and wear. NO masonry, no bricks, no battlements, no arched windows, no carved panels, no gold or bronze bands, no buttress arches, no doors, no stairs, nothing built by people. Only thin faint amber light inside a few deep cracks..

## 2. Size
~30 m tall.

## 3. Look
Natural dark black-brown fractured rock only, the same rock as the ENV-01 hero. Aged bronze only for small fittings (door, posts, braziers, brackets). Warm amber light only inside cracks or where the game uses it. Heavy, rough, weathered. NO built towers: spires, pillars and gates are natural rock.

## 4. Where it is used

Mentioned in: [World and level design](../03-world-and-level-design.md), [Island dressing guide](../16-island-dressing-guide.md), [18. Look Bible](../18-look-bible.md).

## 5. Never
Masonry, bricks, battlements, arched windows, carved panels, gold bands, buttress arches, glossy or chrome surfaces, neon, readable text, skulls, wings, anything that looks built by people unless it is a bronze fitting.

## 6. Pictures, in this order
New Gemini chat for every picture. Attach the approved sheet for this structure (for every picture after the sheet) and the ENV-01 hero for the rock look.

1. **Sheet**: all views in one picture; make this first and keep it
2. **Front**: one picture
3. **3/4 front-left**: one picture

There is no underside view: this stands on the ground (or is far away in the sky), so nobody sees its bottom.

## 7. Not decided yet
Exact size and fine details are proposed. Confirm them when the first sheet is approved.

A GIGANTIC ring of fire that surrounds the ENTIRE floating realm, NOT a small ring on the ground: the whole archipelago of floating rock islands, the bridges and the Throne summit all sit INSIDE the ring, which hangs in open sky at the far edge of the world, kilometers wide, seen from the Throne as a thin glowing circle on the horizon all around. docs/assets/props-catalogue.md:
# Props catalogue: everything Elias gets and carries

> **Proposed.** Free arrows, no ammo sales, no loot boxes. Nothing is bought. Every prop is grounded in the books: Felicia (weapons, ammo, inventory, hidden collectibles), Swink (rules give meaning, no vacuum of pickups, humour as feel), Lovell (generosity, autonomy, relatedness). Elias is the only person in these frames.

## Sacred Arc & Arrows

| ID | Prop | How he gets it | How it is used | Book link |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PRP-01 | **Sacred Arc** | Given on Island 1 (first real pickup) | Draws, aims, fires every arrow type. Never on fire itself. | Felicia: weapons. Swink: one tool, many meanings. |
| PRP-02 | **Quiver** | Starts with it | A well-stocked quiver of about two dozen ordinary arrows plus three sleeves for special arrows; shows which special types he carries, never a number on screen. | Felicia: inventory without a menu. |
| PRP-03 | **Ordinary Arrow** | Free: grows back in the world (arrow bundles in cracks, caches, lantern anchors) | Everyday shot: switches, lanterns, Wraith stagger. | Lovell: generosity. No ammo sales. |
| PRP-04 | **Fire Arrow** | Light any arrow at a brazier, a Cinder ember or flint | Burns cobwebs of ash, lights braziers, scares Wraiths. | Swink: the fire has a rule (it needs a flame to light). |
| PRP-05 | **Rope Arrow** | Find a coil in rock caches | Pins a cord to a far ledge: Elias crosses or climbs it. | Felicia: tools that open space. Climb with a purpose. |
| PRP-06 | **Chain Hook Arrow** | From Island 2 on, in lantern anchors | Hooks a hanging chain to swing a bridge into place. | Swink: object meets rule, no vacuum. |
| PRP-07 | **Lantern Arrow** | Rewarded for freeing a lantern anchor | Lights far lantern anchors; the Eye warms when he does. | Lovell: reward that matters, not a coin. |
| PRP-08 | **Smoke Arrow** | Found in Rock Mage cairns | Wraith loses him for a few breaths: sneak past. | Lovell: challenge vs skill, a stealth option. |
| PRP-09 | **Echo Arrow** | Hidden in alcoves | Draws a Wraith away with a note, or opens a sound door. | Swink: sound need not be real, only meaningful. |
| PRP-10 | **Stone Breaker Arrow** | Sky-Folk Relic cache | Breaks cracked rock: opens a passage, drops a rockfall. | Felicia: hidden collectibles behind hard-to-reach rock. |
| PRP-11 | **Cinder Arrow** | Late: Island 5, after the Cinder bond | Curves around corners to hit what he cannot see. | Swink: late reward changes the feel. |
| PRP-12 | **Gust Arrow** | Wind-cut crevices | Pushes a floating fragment, or slows a fall. | Swink: motion as a gift of the world. |

## Climbing and Tools

| ID | Prop | How he gets it | How it is used | Book link |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PRP-13 | **Climbing Cord** | Starts with a short one; finds longer ones | Lets him rappel into a crevice or tie off a ledge. | Felicia: inventory objects. Stone Passages. |
| PRP-14 | **Wedge Pitons** | Find in rock caches | Wedge into a crack to climb a Chimney or Squeeze. | Lovell: clear skill, clear tool. |
| PRP-15 | **Flint and Steel** | Starts with it | Lights a Fire Arrow if there is no brazier. | Swink: fire only from fire. |
| PRP-16 | **Hand Lantern** | Island 2, from the first lantern anchor | Lights dark passages inside the rock. | Lovell: pottering in dark spaces. |
| PRP-17 | **Water Gourd** | Starts with it | Refills in cloud springs; sip to settle, a calm beat. | Felicia: health items made calm, not a medkit. |
| PRP-18 | **Wrist Wraps** | Starts with it | Grip on rock; they char slowly as the Lines light. | Swink: visible wear as state. |
| PRP-19 | **Cairn Chalk** | Find in Rock Mage cairns | Mark a route on rock so he can return: a small human trace. | Lovell: autonomy. Players mark their own way. |
| PRP-20 | **Ember Needle** | Island 3, from a Sky-Folk Relic | Points toward the Throne, but flickers near danger. | Felicia: guidance without a map marker. |
| PRP-21 | **Hand Torch** | Light at any brazier | Fire in the Stone Passages when the lantern is out. | Swink: a hand-held light changes space. |

## Finds and Keepsakes

| ID | Prop | How he gets it | How it is used | Book link |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PRP-22 | **Memory Shard** | About ten hidden in the world | Watch a short memory; the Eye brightens. | Lovell: hidden reward that means something. |
| PRP-23 | **Lantern Seed** | Found on islands; plant at an anchor | Lights a lantern anchor and changes the sky. | Swink: a physical thing, not a number. |
| PRP-24 | **Arrow Bundle** | Hidden in cracks and caches | Refills the quiver for free. | Lovell: no ammo sales, generosity. |
| PRP-25 | **Sky-Folk Relic** | About twelve hidden in far places | Opens a sealed alcove; unlocks a new arrow. | Felicia: special and hidden collectibles. |
| PRP-26 | **Still Secret** | Appears only if Elias stands still for a count | Reward for stillness: a quiet hint of the Throne. | The Throne of Stillness as a game rule. |
| PRP-27 | **Cairn Gift** | Given by Rock Mages after a calm meeting | Trade for a Smoke Arrow or a path. | Rock Mages as a whole species, friendly. |
| PRP-28 | **Mother Flatbread** | Found only at fires and cairns | Eating it calms the Eye. A quiet, human moment. | Felicia: health pack as comfort, not a bar. |
| PRP-29 | **Wrist Thread** | Starts with it | Shown in memory frames; it glows when a memory is near. | Swink: a small sign of what matters. |
| PRP-30 | **Bronze Key** | Island 1 | Opens the locked door; first real choice. | Felicia: keys and doors. |

## Funny Props

| ID | Prop | How he gets it | How it is used | Book link |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PRP-31 | **Whistling Kettle** | Island 2, from an abandoned camp | Rattles in wind, whistles when a Wraith is near, brews tea at fires. Elias stays deadpan. | Swink: humor as a game feel. Lovell: charm. |
| PRP-32 | **Pocket Pebble Pip** | Starts with it; hidden in Island 1 | Wobbles to look at things; gets lost and found. Never speaks. | Lovell: relatedness. A friend that is an object. |
| PRP-33 | **Boot Bell** | Island 2 | Jingles when he runs: ruins stealth until he muffles it with cloth. | Swink: sound that bites back. |

## Food and Snacks (funny)

| ID | Prop | How he gets it | How it is used | Book link |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PRP-34 | **Cloud Dumpling** | Found at campfires and cairns | He must catch it before it drifts off an island. Eating it makes him float a few steps (a tiny glide). | Swink: a rule that makes a small moment funny. |
| PRP-35 | **Ember Pepper** | Grows in cracks near Lantern Anchors | He sneezes a spark: it can accidentally light a Fire Arrow or a far brazier. Calm face, one raised eyebrow. | Lovell: surprise and delight. |
| PRP-36 | **Stone Soup** | Given by a calmed Rock Mage | He must wait still while it cools. Rock Mages watch. Fully heals the Eye. | Rock Mages as friendly; stillness as the rule. |
| PRP-37 | **Sky Goose Egg** | Hidden on a high ledge | Carry it or eat it. If he carries it, it hatches into a small goose that follows him and honks at Wraiths. | Felicia: hidden collectibles. Lovell: relatedness. |
| PRP-38 | **Sour Cloud Berry** | Cloud springs | A sour wince. Wakes the Eye for a moment. A one second comic beat. | Swink: small feedback gestures. |
| PRP-39 | **Pilfer Snack Pouch** | Starts with it; the bird thief steals it | Chase the bird across islands to get it back. At the end the bird returns it, with a gift. | Lovell: a rival that becomes a friend. |

## Rules

- Arrows are free and come from the world (bundles, caches, lantern anchors). Never sold.
- No HUD: the quiver shows the types he carries.
- A funny prop is only a small beat. Elias stays calm and deadpan, never a broad smile.
- Props are a pickup with a reason, never a vacuum (Swink, Ratchet and Clank warning).
- Premium pay-once game, later DLC could add props. No loot boxes.

docs/assets/fix-plan.md:
# 46. Fix plan: make it a "wow" game (APPROVED)

> **UPDATE 16 Nov:** the owner delegated every decision. **Doc 50 wins where it differs** (food is a fun break given by the living world; no hunger timer; Gravel does not die, he sleeps as stone and wakes; Pilfer Bird and underside are in; three-day clock). Status: APPROVED.

**Written 16 Nov 2026.** The owner asked to fix everything a reviewer would criticise. This page turns each weakness into a concrete change, with the frames and props that carry it. Nothing here deletes an image. Locked rules stay: no HUD, no score, Elias alone until PT-213, sky world only, calm face, natural rock only.

## The six weaknesses and the fix for each

| Weakness a reviewer would write | Fix | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **"Beautiful but empty"** | About 40 hand-placed finds (6 per island), every one with a use, plus the 33 props | Doc 45 section 4, Props catalogue |
| **"Stillness gets boring"** | Stillness changes meaning on every island (table below) so it is a new puzzle each time | Section 1 |
| **"The climb is padding"** | Cut the climb from 14 frames to 8 and fill it with Stone Passages and one new thing per beat | Section 3, Numbers to redo |
| **"Same thing every island"** | One new verb per island: a new arrow, tool or rule | Section 1 |
| **"The world is inconsistent"** | Three canons in every prompt: sky, ring, natural rock | Section 4 |
| **"No moment I will remember"** | Six signature moments only this game can give | Section 2 |

## 1. One new verb per island (and a new meaning for stillness)

| Island | New verb or prop | What stillness means here | Wraith beat |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Starting Shelf | Sacred Arc, Ordinary Arrow, Bronze Key | Stand still and the ember trail shows the way | none (omen only: dust far away) |
| 2 Cinder Garden | Lantern Arrow, Hand Lantern, Whistling Kettle | Stand still so the Cinder settles and lights a path | tiny dust-devil far away |
| 3 Drifting Steps | Echo Arrow, Boot Bell | Stand still on a moving slab so it stops drifting | first stalk: hide behind rock, it passes |
| 4 Arena | Smoke Arrow, Stone Breaker Arrow | Stand still and Rock Mages stack cairns instead of attacking | the big storm |
| 5 Canyon Bridge | Rope Arrow, Chain Hook Arrow | Stand still on the bridge: weight steadies the planks | gale shakes the planks |
| 6 Fragments | Gust Arrow, Climbing Cord | Stand still on a falling rock so it settles | **the chase** (only time he runs) |
| 7 Staircase | Cinder Arrow, Ember Needle | Stand still so the stairs stop shifting | wall of shadow behind him |
| Throne | no new verb: everything he learned | Stillness opens the Eye | the last gust blows out |

Rule: if an island adds no new verb, it is cut or merged (Swink: novelty; Lovell: flow zone).

## 2. Six signature moments (the sentences in the review)

1. **The tired Eye.** Rush and the Eye droops and weeps amber light, the world dims. Rest and it wakes and shows a memory. No number, no scolding.
2. **The kettle whistles.** On Island 2 the Whistling Kettle screams at a far Wraith. Elias stays deadpan. The funny beat the game needs.
3. **The Rock Mages stack cairns.** The enemy that stops being an enemy when you are still.
4. **The chase on Island 6.** The ground vanishes behind him; the only time he runs. Everything else is calm, so this lands.
5. **The glass shadow breaks.** The vision of his own broken self, ending in glass falling apart.
6. **The ring ignites.** One closed ring of fire around the whole realm, then the islands rejoin and the people return.

## 3. Shorten the climb, make it a place not a staircase

Keep: 189 (the stairs), 190 (the cloak), 192 (his mother), 193 (his face), 194 (the cairn guard), 195 (Line 6 ignites), 196 and 197 (the dragon). Merge or skip: 191, 199, 200, 201, 202. Replace the long middle with two **Stone Passages** (chimney, squeeze) and one **find** (a Sky-Folk Relic), so every minute has something new. Target climb: 8 frames, about 12 minutes.

## 4. Three canons put into every prompt

- **Sky:** warm pale-gold daylight, white clouds below, brighter by a little with each Line lit, never storm-black. Only caves and the glass duel are dark.
- **Ring of Fire:** one huge closed ring around the whole floating realm at the far edge of the world, a dark ember line until the Throne.
- **Natural rock:** no castles, towers, masonry or arched windows; bronze bridges, chains, lantern anchors and rock ruins only.

These are already appended to the 63 frames on the "Numbers to redo" page.

## 5. Game feel (Swink) so it is good in the hands, not only on screen

- A hit-pause of about 20 ms and light camera shake when a Rock Mage slams or the Wraith passes.
- Controller rumble that matches the metaphor: stone is a low rumble, wind is a soft hiss, the Eye is a slow heartbeat.
- A strange, non-real sound for the Eye and the Wraith.
- A tiny Elias next to every huge thing (Dragon, Throne, Wraith) for the impression of size.

## 6. Order of work

1. **Now (done in the hub):** props, numbers to redo, canon paragraphs in prompts.
2. **Next:** write PT-221 onward (about 70 frames): the Eye states, the Wraith beats, the finds, the Stone Passages, the new arrows in use.
3. **Then:** write ENV-14, 15, 16 (passage blueprints) and update core systems.
4. **Then:** one island as a playable test (Island 1 or 3) to check game feel, because only play shows if it is fun.
5. **Then:** regenerate the redo frames, starting with the motion and sky ones.

## 7. Target review

> A calm, strange, beautiful game about stopping. The Eye that droops when you rush and wakes when you rest is something I have not seen. Every island gave me a new tool, the chase on the fragments had me gripping the controller, and the ending made me feel something.

The review we are avoiding: "Gorgeous but empty, the climb drags, and stillness gets repetitive."
docs/assets/youtuber-test.md:
# 47. The YouTuber test: surprise, variety and "oh wow" (APPROVED)

> **UPDATE 16 Nov:** the owner delegated every decision. **Doc 50 wins where it differs** (food is a fun break given by the living world; no hunger timer; Gravel does not die, he sleeps as stone and wakes; Pilfer Bird and underside are in; three-day clock). Status: APPROVED.

**Written 16 Nov 2026.** The owner imagined a pro gamer playing the game on camera and saying: "he picks up arrows, he fights, he stands still, he fights, he stands still, he goes to the Throne, no originality, dull." This page is the cure. It is blunt on purpose: **the plan in docs 45 and 46 was safe.** It fixed the holes but did not add surprise. This page adds it.

## 1. Why the player would get bored (the honest diagnosis)

- The core loop is **fight, then stand still, then fight, then stand still.** Even a beautiful loop is a loop. A viewer sees the pattern in 15 minutes.
- Every island asks the same question. A new arrow is a new tool, not a new feeling.
- The player is never **surprised by the game.** Nothing ever goes wrong in a way that is funny, scary or strange.
- Elias has no needs. A hero who never gets hungry, tired or robbed is a hero nothing happens to.

## 2. The rule that fixes it: the ten-minute budget

**Every ten minutes of play must contain all six of these.** If a ten-minute block lacks one, it gets redesigned.

| Beat | What the viewer says |
|---|---|
| **One new thing** (a tool, a creature, a rule) | "Oh, what is that?" |
| **One surprise** (the game breaks its own pattern) | "I did NOT expect that!" |
| **One laugh** | "Ha, did you see that?" |
| **One scare or pressure** | "What am I going to do?!" |
| **One quiet beauty** | "Oh wow, look at this." |
| **One discovery that is the player's own** | "Oh my God, I found something!" |

## 3. Break the loop: stillness stops being the answer

Stillness stays the soul of the game, but **it must sometimes be the wrong answer**, so the player has to read the situation.

| Situation | Stillness | The twist |
|---|---|---|
| Wraith of dust | Right (it passes) | classic |
| **The Hungry Gale** | WRONG: it hunts what stands still, so he must keep moving | inversion |
| **Mirror Island** | Freezes the island; moving rewinds it | time puzzle |
| **Quiet Island** | The sound drops out; he plays by ember light and feel | sense change |
| **Bat-bird flock** | Wrong alone, right with the Echo Arrow: still while the arrow draws them away | combo |
| **The Sleeping Giant** | Right at first; then it wakes and he must ride it | set piece |

No two consecutive fights may be solved the same way.

## 4. Falling, gliding and flying are the game, not the failure

- **The cloak is a glider.** Jump from an island and the cloak catches the air. Falling and gliding between islands is a core move, so "Oh wow, I'm falling, oh wow, I'm flying" happens in every hour.
- **Falling is a discovery.** Fall through the clouds and you do not die: you land on an **underside island** (lantern gardens hanging upside down, old sky-folk ruins, a hidden Memory Shard). A fall is a different path, not a fail screen.
- **Updrafts and the Gust Arrow** make flight a puzzle: find the wind, ride the wind.
- **The Fire Dragon** appears early as a surprise rescue (it catches him mid-fall), then returns as a ride.

## 5. Hunger, rest and food (a funny system that makes him human)

Yes: he needs to eat, and it should be funny.

- **No HUD.** Hunger is told by his stomach growling, Cinder nagging, and a slight sway in the camera.
- **Eating is a scene, not a menu.** He sits, the Eye wakes, and the food does something silly. His face stays calm and deadpan: one raised eyebrow, never a broad smile.
- **Foods in the Props catalogue:** Cloud Dumpling (floats away, he chases it), Ember Pepper (he sneezes sparks that light a far brazier), Stone Soup (a Rock Mage gift, he must sit still while it cools), Sky Goose Egg (hatches into a goose that follows him and honks at Wraiths), Sour Cloud Berry (a sour wince), and Mother's Flatbread (the quiet one that wakes a memory).
- **The Pilfer Bird** steals his snack pouch on Island 2. He chases it across islands ("this bird is attacking me!"). It becomes a friend and returns the pouch at the Throne.
- **Rest is a pleasure:** a campfire evening between big parts, with the food gag, a memory on the Eye and a view of the stars.

## 6. Time: one day or a month? Three days and nights

**Recommendation: three days and nights, from dawn to dawn.** A month would blunt the urgency and make hunger a chore. One day is too short for rest and hunger.

| Time | Place | Sky |
|---|---|---|
| Dawn, day 1 | Islands 1 to 3 | soft golden dawn, low sun |
| Dusk, day 1 | Arena | orange sunset, first campfire meal |
| Night, day 1 to 2 | Rest at a lantern anchor | stars and moons, lanterns glowing |
| Day 2 | Canyon and Fragments | bright noon, then storm gold |
| Night 2 | Rest in the Staircase caves | deep blue, Eye bright |
| Dawn, day 3 | Climb and Throne | the dawn that opens the movie, now closed as a circle |

This also **fixes the sky inconsistency for good**: the sky is a clock, so dark and light frames are intentional, not random. (If you approve this, I will rewrite the sky canon in the redo prompts from "always daylight" to "the time of day of this island".)

## 7. Surprises only this game can have (the sentences a YouTuber says)

1. **The false Throne.** On Island 5 he finds a Throne. He sits. The Eye weeps: "not yet". It was a tomb of someone who stopped too early.
2. **The Glass Shadow copies how YOU played** (arrow user, runner, still-sitter) and fights you that way.
3. **The Sleeping Giant wakes** and you travel across the sky on its back for ten minutes.
4. **Rock Mages stack a cairn tower that spells a path** and a bird lands on top.
5. **The kettle whistles at a Wraith** and the Wraith flinches.
6. **A hidden ending** if every Sky-Folk Relic is found: the Throne room contains the people who lived before.
7. **The underside world** under the clouds, a second world nobody told you about.

## 8. Do I need your books and games?

Honestly: **I can design this myself, but I will be better with your references**, and the first version was safe because I stayed inside the books and the locked rules. Three ways to help:
- **Games you love** (clips or names). I will break down why each one makes players shout, not copy them. Good starting list: Outer Wilds (discovery nobody told you about), A Short Hike (gliding, birds, small funny moments, food), Journey (wordless wonder), Sky: Children of the Light (flight in a cloud world), Breath of the Wild (every rock is a question), Shadow of the Colossus (riding giants).
- **YouTube reactions** to games you wish ours matched. I will list the exact moments people react to.
- **Books** on pacing, level design or humor, if you have them.

## 9. Order of work

1. You decide: three days and nights, the false Throne, the hunger system, the Pilfer Bird, "stillness sometimes wrong".
2. I write a **first 30 minutes, minute by minute**, so you can judge it as a viewer would.
3. I add the new frames (Eye, Wraith, finds, food, bird thief, underside world, false Throne) from PT-221.
4. We build one island as a playable test.

# 48. Emotion and depth: from "pretty and childish" to "a movie" (APPROVED)

> **UPDATE 16 Nov:** the owner delegated every decision. **Doc 50 wins where it differs** (food is a fun break given by the living world; no hunger timer; Gravel does not die, he sleeps as stone and wakes; Pilfer Bird and underside are in; three-day clock). Status: APPROVED.

**Written 16 Nov 2026.** The owner wants the feeling of a film like *Dune*: things change, and the story goes through wonder, loneliness, anger, love and frustration. Food stays. This page adds the emotional spine, a friend, a talking inner voice, and the reading list.

## 1. The emotional arc across three days

| Day | Feeling | What the player does | Peak moment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Day 1 (dawn to dusk)** | Wonder, then loneliness | Learns the world. Quiet islands. First campfire alone | He talks to the empty air and Pebble Pip |
| **Day 2** | Frustration, then **anger** | The chase, the false Throne, the broken bow | He shoots an arrow at the Eye in rage. It weeps. The game gives him no help for a while |
| **Day 3 (dawn)** | Grief, forgiveness, **love** | The climb, his mother, the ring | He says what he could not say. The Throne |

Rule: **no ten-minute block stays in one emotion.** *Dune* works because beauty, dread and tenderness alternate.

## 2. A friend (so he is not only fighting stones)

Elias is alone among people until PT-213, so the friend is **not a person**. It is a Rock Mage, the approved species (CRE-04).
- **Gravel** (working name): a small, young Rock Mage who stacks stones into cairns. He first watches Elias from far away on Island 4.
- He cannot speak. He **talks in cairns**: a stack of three stones means "come", a leaning stack means "careful", a stack with a flower means "thank you".
- He carries Elias across a gap, shares Stone Soup, and teaches the player what the cairns mean.
- **The loss:** on the Staircase he holds the stone stair together so Elias can climb, and crumbles into a cairn at the top. Every cairn the player passed earlier now reads as his. A quiet, devastating beat. (Needs your approval: it is the one real sadness in the game.)
- Other companions stay light: the Pilfer Bird (rival, then friend), the Sky Goose (comic), the Cinder (guide, then something more).

## 3. Elias talks (his inner voice)

About **40 spoken lines in the whole game**, never a long speech, never narration of what the player can see. Dry, calm, sometimes funny. Examples:
- Waking after a cold night: "Still here. Good."
- Missing a jump: "That was the plan." (deadpan)
- After three days without washing, at a cloud spring: "I smell like a burnt boot."
- To the kettle: "Not now." (when it whistles at the wrong time)
- To the Eye after the rage: "I'm sorry." (the only time his voice breaks)
- To the empty sky at night: "Mother, I'm still climbing."

Rules: his face stays calm. A joke is a dry line, not a grin. A line that explains the puzzle is cut.

## 4. Anger, frustration and loneliness as game moments, not cutscenes

- **Loneliness:** the **Quiet Island**. The music drops out. Only wind and his breathing. No Cinder, no kettle. A long empty vista. It must be earned and short (3 minutes).
- **Frustration:** the **Sacred Arc string snaps** on Day 2. He repairs it with the **Wrist Thread** from his mother. Until he does, he has no bow: the player must climb and sneak. The prop pays off the story.
- **Anger:** after the false Throne, the player may fire an arrow at the Eye. If they do, the Eye weeps and the world dims for a few minutes. If they do not, the Eye still weeps, but quieter. Either way it is the player's choice, and the game remembers it in the ending.
- **Love:** the memory scenes (his mother's last night) play in the Eye, and **one of them is interactive**: he can hold the memory still, or he can reach for it and it dissolves.
- **Guilt and forgiveness:** at the Throne, the Eye shows the truth (PT-213). The ending changes slightly depending on whether he raged at the Eye.

## 5. The *Dune* craft list (what makes it feel like a film)

- **Scale and silence.** Huge things, long shots, then nothing. Always put a tiny Elias next to the huge thing.
- **A long breath after every big beat.** A 20 to 30 second walk with no objective.
- **Ritual.** The same small gesture repeated, then broken: he always lights a lantern before sleeping; the one night he cannot, it matters.
- **A threat that is never fully explained.** The Wraith.
- **Costume and light as story.** His suit glow dims when he is tired, scorches when he rages, brightens with the Lines.
- **A score with two themes:** his theme (alone) and the Eye's theme. At the end they play together.

## 6. The reading list (what to read and why)

I found these through searches of recommended-reading lists (links at the end); the picks and the reasons are mine.

**Emotion and player experience**
- **Katherine Isbister, *How Games Move Us*.** Exactly your question: how designers evoke strong emotions. The source for the friend, loss and loneliness beats.
- **Jesse Schell, *The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses*.** 100+ lenses (questions) to test any idea. Use it as a checklist on every island.
- **Raph Koster, *A Theory of Fun for Game Design*.** Why a loop goes stale (your "fight, still, fight, still" worry). The cure is new patterns to learn.
- **James Paul Gee, *What Video Games Have to Teach Us About Learning and Literacy*.** A low-stakes space where failing is safe: the basis of "falling is a discovery".
- **Steve Swink, *Game Feel*** and **Nicholas Lovell, *The Pyramid of Game Design*** (already in your Project).

**Story and film craft (for the *Dune* feeling)**
- **Robert McKee, *Story*** and **John Truby, *The Anatomy of Story*.** Turn a plot into an emotional arc and a hero's flaw.
- **Christopher Vogler, *The Writer's Journey*** and **Joseph Campbell, *The Hero with a Thousand Faces*.** The myth structure your story already follows (the call, the threshold, the abyss, the return).
- **Tanya Lapointe, *The Art and Soul of Dune*.** How the film makers built scale, silence and mood (note: a book I know of, not one I found in the searches).

**How hits really get made**
- **Jason Schreier, *Blood, Sweat, and Pixels*.** Real stories of how great and troubled games were made. Good for avoiding common production traps.
- **Scott Rogers, *Level Up!*.** Practical guide to set pieces, enemies and pacing.

## 7. Where reviewers say what they love and hate

- **Game Maker's Toolkit** (Mark Brown), **Noclip** documentaries and **Extra Credits** (YouTube): design breakdowns of games like Journey, Outer Wilds and Shadow of the Colossus.
- **GDC talks** (free on the GDC YouTube channel): postmortems from the developers of Journey, Outer Wilds, A Short Hike and others, including what failed.
- **Steam itself.** Sort the negative reviews of games like ours (Outer Wilds, A Short Hike, Journey, Sky: Children of the Light, Ico, Shadow of the Colossus). The complaints are free design advice.
- **One study I found** analysed 4,856 Steam and Quest games using review text. It reports that players praise **graphics and audio** most, and complain most about **difficulty, controls, replayability and monetization**. That supports your choices: premium price, no microtransactions, a strong look, and care with difficulty. Caveat: the scoring was checked on only one game's reviews, so treat it as a hint.

## 8. Next steps

1. You send me the games and reviewers you love. I will pull what players say they love and hate in each and turn it into a "do and don't" list for this game.
2. You approve the emotional spine (Gravel the friend and his loss, the snapped string, the arrow at the Eye, the inner voice).
3. I write the first 30 minutes minute by minute, then the new frames from PT-221.

**Sources:** [10 Great Books for Game Designers (80.lv)](https://80.lv/articles/10-great-books-for-game-designers/), [Katherine Isbister's five best books on video games (Five Books)](https://fivebooks.com/best-books/katherine-isbister-video-games/), [Steam and Quest review analysis (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.16596v5), [Best game design books (Shortform)](https://www.shortform.com/best-books/genre/best-game-design-books-of-all-time).

# 49. Book harvest: what six books change in I-RULE01 (APPROVED)

> **UPDATE 16 Nov:** the owner delegated every decision. **Doc 50 wins where it differs** (food is a fun break given by the living world; no hunger timer; Gravel does not die, he sleeps as stone and wakes; Pilfer Bird and underside are in; three-day clock). Status: APPROVED.

**Written 16 Nov 2026.** Sources: *A Theory of Fun* (Koster), *The Art of Game Design* (Schell), *The Anatomy of Story* (Truby), *How Games Move Us* (Isbister), *Level Up!* (Rogers), *Blood, Sweat, and Pixels* (Schreier). Everything below is a **proposal**. Nothing here overrides docs 41 to 48 until you approve it. Where a book already agrees with something we decided, it says so.

## 1. The fourteen rules we adopt

1. **One lesson.** Fun is learning a pattern (Koster). Our lesson is the owner's own: **slow down and listen, stillness wins.** Every system must teach it or support it. A system that does not gets cut (Koster, Schell "Inner Contradiction").
2. **Boredom is a signal.** If a player is bored, the game has stopped teaching. Fix the lesson, not the decoration (Koster).
3. **Delight = a pattern the player knows plus one wrinkle they did not expect** (Koster). Every island: one known verb, one new wrinkle.
4. **Interest curve, not a flat line.** Hook, rise with small peaks, a quiet trough before each big peak, a climax, then a calm ending (Schell, Lens 61). Section 3.
5. **Every island ends with a question** (Schell, Lens of Curiosity). Section 3.
6. **Give the player ways to surprise themselves** (Schell, Lens of Surprise). Tricks they find that we never told them about.
7. **Only one corner of the Triangle of Weirdness** (Rogers). Our world is the weird corner. So the people, their wishes and the activities stay familiar: climbing, aiming, being hungry, being lonely. See section 6.
8. **Awe comes from being small** (Isbister on *Journey*). Elias stays tiny against huge shapes. No power fantasy shots.
9. **Responsiveness is emotion.** Jump, glide, draw the bow: the feel of the movement is half the feeling (Isbister, Rogers, and Swink from before).
10. **Companions are loved through humour, shared struggle and loss** (Isbister on Floyd in *Planetfall*). Gravel follows all three.
11. **Chekhov's gun.** Every prop shown early pays off later (Rogers). Section 6.
12. **Death must matter, but never waste the player's time** (Rogers, Koster "failure has a cost").
13. **One vertical slice first.** One island, finished, before building the rest (Schreier). Section 8.
14. **Cut early, cut kindly.** The best games lose features (Schreier on *Uncharted 4*). Section 8 has our cut list.

## 2. A Theory of Fun (Koster): what it adds

- **The atoms checklist** (every island must have): preparation, sense of space, a core mechanic, a range of challenges, a range of abilities, skill in using those abilities, variable feedback, a mastery problem, and failure with a cost. Section 7 turns it into a per-island test.
- **Flow zone:** challenge rises with skill. Our ten-minute budget (doc 47) is how we keep Elias in it.
- **Games rarely show the human condition.** His examples: the **loneliness of being at the top**, and friends falling away as power rises. That is exactly the Throne: the more he climbs, the fewer people are left (the Gravel loss, doc 48). Keep it as the quiet theme, never said out loud.
- **Social emotions to aim for:** *fiero* (triumph over hardship), *naches* (pride in someone you raised), *kvell* (pride shown in public). Gravel gives the second: Elias teaches Gravel to use the bow's string, and later Gravel's cairns teach Elias. The final ring gives the first.
- **Grooming and feeding** are how social animals bond. This is the real reason the food scenes work: sharing Stone Soup with Gravel is bonding, not a gag.
- **Designeritis:** designers copy other games. Steal from outside games: mountaineering, shepherds, cairn-building, desert caravans, *Dune*.
- **Test the game with no graphics, no sound, no story.** If the grey-box island is still fun, the art will lift it. Section 8.
- **Innovation = add one new dimension.** Ours is the **underside** of the islands and falling as a way to travel (doc 47).

## 3. The Art of Game Design (Schell): what it adds

**The lenses that matter most for this game:**

| Lens | What it asks | What we do |
|---|---|---|
| **2 Surprise** | Do rules let players surprise themselves? | Cloak glide, arrow tricks (Echo, Smoke, Rope) found by play, never by tutorial. |
| **4 Curiosity** | What questions does the game put in the player's mind? | Each island closes with a question (below). |
| **61 Interest curve** | Hook, rise, peaks, trough, climax, ending | Per-island table below. |
| **69 Weirdest Thing** | What is the one weird thing, and does it confuse? | The weirdest thing is the Eye that remembers. Everything else is plain. |
| **82 Inner Contradiction** | Does anything in the game defeat its purpose? | Rule 1. A hunger timer that rushes the player contradicts "slow down", so hunger **must never be a countdown** (see section 10). |
| **81 Character transformation** | Does each character change, believably? | Elias, the Eye, Gravel and the Cinder each get one visible change. |
| **84 Friendship** and **88 Love** | How do friends form, and does the team love it? | Gravel: meets, is wary, shares food, sacrifices himself. |
| **63 Beauty** | Is every element beautiful, and the combination poetic? | One frame per island is a "silence frame" held for 5 seconds with no UI. |
| **97 Transformation** | How does the game change the player? | He should leave calmer and slower. The ending credits roll with no input. |
| **100 Secret Purpose** | What is the real reason the designer makes this? | Yours: to show that you win by being still. It is in the file name *Stillness Wins*. Keep it secret from the player, not from the team. |

**Interest curve for the whole game (three days):**

| Part | Shape | Beat |
|---|---|---|
| First 60 seconds | **Hook** | Elias is awake on a cold ledge, the Eye is visible, a bird steals something. |
| Islands 1 to 3 | Rising small peaks | New tool on each island, one laugh, one scare. |
| Island 4 | Peak, then trough | Gravel is met. Quiet afterward. |
| Island 5 | **False peak** | The false Throne. Anger. |
| Island 6 | Deep trough then climb | Quiet Island, then the snapped string. |
| Island 7 | Big peak | The chase, the Wraith. |
| Staircase | **Climax** | Gravel's sacrifice. |
| Throne | Release | The ring, his mother. |

**Island-closing questions** (placement can move): What does the Eye remember? Who stacked these cairns? Why do the Relics glow near him? What is under the island? Why does the kettle whistle at nothing? Who is the second light on the far side?

**Hero's Journey check** (Vogler's twelve steps, used as a checklist only): Ordinary World (the village before the break), Call (the whisper), Refusal (he rushes alone), Mentor (Cinder), Threshold (Island 1), Tests/Allies/Enemies (Islands 2 to 4), Approach (Island 5), Ordeal (Island 6 and the Staircase), Reward (the Throne), Road Back (ring), Resurrection (stillness), Return with the Elixir (the new fire). It fits. We do not stage it in order of the book, we only check nothing is missing.

## 4. The Anatomy of Story (Truby): Elias as a Truby hero

*Canon notes: the parents' deaths, the whispers and the promise of the fire are unchanged. Wraith as "his own rush" is a PROPOSAL.*

| Truby step | I-RULE01 |
|---|---|
| **Weakness** | He rushes, hides fear behind a calm face and cannot say goodbye. |
| **Need (psychological)** | To slow down and listen. |
| **Need (moral)** | To forgive, himself and the broken world (the Eye). |
| **Desire** | Reach the Throne and light the fire. |
| **Opponent** | The Wraith: a dark copy that is **faster** than him. It is not good against evil; it is the same wish done wrong (Truby: hero and opponent share traits). |
| **Plan** | Climb fast, shoot first. |
| **Apparent defeat** | The false Throne (Island 5) and the snapped string. |
| **Visit to death** | The Staircase, where Gravel dies. |
| **Battle** | The narrowest place in the game: the Staircase top. Truby says the battle happens in the most confined space. |
| **Self-revelation** | Stillness is not waiting, it is listening. |
| **Moral decision** | At the top he **chooses to stop** instead of rushing the last step. |
| **New equilibrium** | The ring. The fire is lit by breath, not by an arrow. |

- **Designing principle** (one sentence, Truby): *A rushing boy learns stillness by climbing seven floating islands in three days, one breath at a time.* If a scene does not serve this sentence, cut it.
- **Symbol web (refer and repeat):** the **cairn** (a path marker, then Gravel, then the marker at the top); the **thread** (Wrist Thread, repairs the snapped string, ties the last arrow); the **breath** (the first fire is lit by breath). Each symbol appears three times, slightly changed each time.
- **Miniatures:** each island is a small, readable model of the whole world. The village before the break is the model of the whole story.
- **Character web:** Elias (hero), Wraith (opponent), Cinder (ally and fake-opponent), Gravel (ally), the Eye (opponent who becomes ally), the mother's whisper (mentor). Each is a different answer to "how do you climb?"
- **Moral argument:** is it better to arrive first or arrive whole? The Wraith says first.

## 5. How Games Move Us (Isbister): feelings by design

- **Awe by smallness (*Journey*):** small robed figure, huge sparse landscape, a long scarf. Subtle **marks of experience** appear on the cloak as you progress. For us: soot and a mended string appear on Elias's coat and bow, and nothing else changes.
- **Movement is emotion:** a reviewer says jumping in *Journey* feels like "a soul freed of its corporeal baggage". Our cloak glide and the draw of the Sacred Arc get the same care (Swink's rules, already in the build list).
- **Wordless collaboration:** *Journey*'s travellers say nothing and still become attached. Gravel talks only in cairns. This is the right call.
- **Floyd (*Planetfall*):** a companion who is funny, helpful, then sacrifices himself, remembered for decades. Gravel follows this recipe: **funny, useful, gone.** Isbister notes the strongest NPC feelings come from subtle social cues (looking at you, waiting for you, reacting to your choices).
- **Responsibility for something fragile (*Hush*):** caring for a baby makes the player care. For us: on Island 6 Elias **carries a Lantern Seed** that must be kept alive, shielded in his coat from wind. Short, optional to repeat.
- **Empathy through ordinary work (*Cart Life*):** chores make people real. Camp is Elias's chore scene: tend fire, mend string, eat. It is where we are allowed to be quiet.
- **Complicity (*Train*):** guilt comes from the player's own action. The optional **arrow at the Eye** (doc 48) is that moment. He chose it; the game remembers.
- **Flow zone (Jenova Chen):** same as Koster. Keep challenge matched to skill.

## 6. Level Up! (Rogers): practical rules

- **Triangle of Weirdness.** Pick one: weird characters, weird activities, or weird world. Choose more than one and you alienate people. *Star Wars* is a weird world with familiar people and wishes. **I-RULE01 is a weird world.** So: Elias wants something everyone understands, Gravel wants not to be alone, and the activities (climb, shoot, eat, rest) are ordinary. The funny props must be funny in a human way (hunger, smell, cold), not in a strange-species way. *Dune* (1984) is Rogers's example of going too far.
- **Chekhov's gun.** Show everything the player needs; every prop shown early must be used. Pay-offs: the **Whistling Kettle** whistles at the Wraith; the **Wrist Thread** repairs the string; the **Bronze Key** opens the Sleeping Giant door; the **Cairn Chalk** marks the way back.
- **Idles.** An idle is an animation that plays when the player stops. It gives personality for free. Elias idles (each under 4 seconds): checks the bowstring, sniffs his sleeve, shivers, nods to the empty air, rubs his wrist. **A long idle triggers the mother's whisper**, which rewards stillness, our lesson.
- **Praise the player.** *Wiki* in a puzzle game gets eight layers of praise for one solved puzzle. We use one or two for big finds only (a sound, a glow, Elias's line), never for every pickup.
- **Boss design.** Three kinds: *learned moves* (uses what the player knows), *new ability* (introduces a tool), or a combination staged with one emphasised. "If they can do it, they should have it" (form follows function). A boss should represent something to the hero. Ours: Island bosses use learned moves, the Wraith uses stillness itself as the weapon.
- **Character functions list** (Rogers's trick): hero (Elias), mentor (the whisper and Cinder), assistant (Pip), tutor (cairns), final boss (Wraith), minions (Shadows), bosses (Hungry Gale, Glass Shadow, Sleeping Giant), hostage (the Eye). Nothing is missing.
- **Camera and controls.** Never lose the character; a bad camera ends a game faster than anything. Third person, no camera fights on narrow ledges, an auto-tilt on drops.
- **Death matters.** Failure costs a little and wastes nothing: retry within 3 seconds, small loss (arrow count, a minute of food), never a lost island.
- **Rule of three** for every list and pitch, and a **ten-pager** (title, concept, story, gameplay, world, characters, screenshots, USPs) for the Steam page and any publisher.
- **A game's "everything is liquid".** The design doc changes. Keep docs short and current.
- **Never dismiss a silly idea.** Rogers's list: a hungry yellow disc, a plumber jumping on mushrooms. The kettle that whistles stays.

## 7. Per-island test (apply to Islands 1 to 7 and the Throne)

An island is **not done** until every line is yes:

| Check | Source |
|---|---|
| Is there **one verb the player already knows** and **one new wrinkle**? | Koster delight |
| Is there a **preparation** (the player sees the problem before attempting it)? | Koster atoms |
| Does it have a **range of challenges** from easy to hard, with variable feedback? | Koster atoms |
| Is there **one surprise the player finds on their own**? | Schell Lens 2 |
| Is there **one laugh**, **one scare**, **one silence frame**? | doc 47 ten-minute budget |
| Does **failure cost something small** and restart fast? | Koster, Rogers |
| Does **Elias say one line** (or deliberately none)? | doc 48 |
| Does it end on a **question**? | Schell Lens 4 |
| Does it **serve the one lesson**? If not, **cut it**. | Koster, Schell Lens 82 |
| Does it work **in grey-box, with no art or sound**? | Koster |

## 8. Blood, Sweat, and Pixels (Schreier): production lessons

- **Scope kills.** *Pillars of Eternity* and *Dragon Age: Inquisition* both fought scope all the way to launch. Seven islands of unforgettable content beat ten of average content, so the cut list is real.
- **Vertical slice first.** A small piece that looks and plays like the final game. **Our slice = Island 1**, grey-boxed in UE5: climb, arrow, glide, one laugh, one silence frame, the Eye. It is also the **Steam Next Fest demo** (10 minutes).
- **Prototype with grey boxes.** *Uncharted 4* tried a slide, bullet-hole climbing and a ballroom dance, and cut most. We prototype the false Throne, the cloak glide and the hunger system in grey-box first and keep only what is fun.
- **Constraints are design.** *Shovel Knight* set itself NES rules. Our rules: three arrow types at a time, one tool slot, no inventory screen.
- **One person can finish.** *Stardew Valley* was made by one man over years. It works because he built what he felt strongly about and refused to add features that did not belong. Keep the team small.
- **Crunch ruins people.** Plan buffers; schedule the vertical slice in weeks, not days.
- **Talk to fans early, but guard the vision.** Kickstarter backers saw *Pillars* constantly. We show the slice, not a promise.

**Our cut list** (ordered, from first to cut):
- *Tier A (must ship):* Islands 1 to 7, Throne, arrows, cloak glide, Eye, Wraith, Gravel, food, camp, ring.
- *Tier B (ship if the slice is fun):* underside world, Pilfer Bird, hidden ending, Sleeping Giant ride.
- *Tier C (post-launch):* extra relics, photo mode, speed-run mode.

## 9. What this adds to the build list

| Item | Source | Size |
|---|---|---|
| **Quiet Director:** a small state machine that watches stress (deaths, time since a quiet beat) and triggers or delays a bird raid, gust or food scene, like the *Left 4 Dead* Director Rogers describes | Rogers | small |
| Elias idle set (6 animations) and the idle-whisper rule | Rogers | small |
| Lantern Seed care mission on Island 6 | Isbister | small |
| Symbol web (cairn, thread, breath) placed in a table, 3 appearances each | Truby | doc only |
| Designing-principle sentence pinned in every doc header | Truby | doc only |
| One-lesson audit of every system | Koster | doc only |
| Per-island test (section 7) in each island brief | Koster, Schell | doc only |
| Vertical slice and Next Fest demo plan | Schreier | planning |
| Ten-pager for the Steam page | Rogers | writing |
| Cloak, coat and bow wear marks across the three days | Isbister | art, small |

## 10. Decisions I need from you

1. **Hunger as a mood, not a clock.** Per Lens 82, no countdown. Hunger changes how Elias moves and talks, and food is a comfort scene. Approve?
2. **The Wraith as "his own rushing"** (a dark copy that is faster than him) rather than a separate evil. This is Truby's strongest tool. Approve?
3. **Gravel's name and death** (carried over from doc 48). Still approved?
4. **The cut list in section 8**, especially: are the Pilfer Bird and the underside world Tier B?

## 11. Sources

- Koster, *A Theory of Fun for Game Design*.
- Schell, *The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses* (Lens numbers are as in the book).
- Truby, *The Anatomy of Story: 22 Steps to Becoming a Master Storyteller*.
- Isbister, *How Games Move Us: Emotion by Design*.
- Rogers, *Level Up! The Guide to Great Video Game Design*.
- Schreier, *Blood, Sweat, and Pixels*.

# 50. Decisions made and Playthrough v3 (APPROVED: owner said "decide and I will tell you later")

**16 Nov 2026.** You asked me to decide everything and build. This page settles every open question from docs 45 to 49 and adds **63 new playthrough frames (PT-221 to PT-283)** and **4 new creature sheets (CRE-11 Gravel, CRE-12 Pilfer Bird, CRE-13 The Wraith, CRE-14 Bat-Bird)**. **Where doc 50 disagrees with docs 45 to 49, doc 50 wins.** Tell me what you do not like and I will change it.

## 1. The decisions

| Question | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Food** | Food is **not a comfort scene**. It is a **fun break and a gag**, and **the living world gives it**. The rock opens a warm bowl of soup, a bush leans down with berries, a cloud curls into a dumpling, a pepper plant sneezes sparks, a goose rolls an egg to him. Everything here is alive, so the world looks after him. | Your words. It is also Isbister's point that small chores make a world feel real, and Koster's point that sharing food is bonding. |
| **Hunger** | **No hunger timer, ever.** Elias gets hungry in a line of dialogue and the world offers food at the quiet moments the Quiet Director picks. Nothing punishes him for not eating. | A countdown would make him rush, and our lesson is "slow down" (Schell, Lens of Inner Contradiction). |
| **The Wraith** | In plain words: **a dark copy of Elias that appears when he hurries.** His own shadow runs a half second ahead of him, then stands up and chases him. It is faster than he is. It fades **only when he stands still.** There is no separate evil villain. | The best enemy is the hero's own weakness (Truby). It teaches the lesson without a speech. |
| **Gravel** | Approved. **He does not die.** On the Staircase he holds the stairs up and settles into a cairn of three stones, still faintly glowing. When the Ring lights, the cairn **stands up** and Gravel wakes. A sad moment that ends well. | You said "no death, let it be." This keeps the loneliness theme (Koster) and the sacrifice beat (Floyd, Isbister) without a loss the player cannot undo. |
| **Pilfer Bird** | **In (Tier A).** Thief, then rival, then friend. It steals the Arrow Bundle in Stage 1 and returns it, with a Memory Shard, in the underside. | Gives a running gag and a second small friend. |
| **Underside world** | **In (Tier A).** You fall through a brittle slab and land under the island, in a glowing hanging forest. | It is the "new dimension" (Koster) and a big surprise for a reviewer. |
| **Hidden ending** | In. A door under the Throne, opened by the Bronze Key. | A reward for exploring. |
| **False Throne** | In, at the end of Stage 5, followed by the snapped string and the arrow at the Eye. | Anger beat. |
| **Eye** | Healthy: it shows **memory films** on the clouds. Hurt or tired: dim, half-closed, ash on the lid. **Optional rage arrow** makes it weep. Elias says "I'm sorry." and it stays dim until the Wrist Thread repair. | Your idea, with a consequence. |
| **Stillness** | Right at the Wraith, the Giant, the shadow duel and the Throne. **Wrong** at the Hungry Gale, Mirror Island and the bat-birds. | Variety: the player must read the situation, not repeat one trick. |
| **Cloak glide** | In. Discovered by the player, never taught. | Surprise they find for themselves (Schell). |
| **Three days** | Approved. Day 1 dawn to night, Day 2 morning to night, Day 3 dawn to the Throne. | A reviewer needs a sense of a journey and of time. |
| **Sky canon** | **Replaced.** The sky always has the same things (cloud sea, planets, two moons, floating islands), but **the light follows the clock** (table below). Never storm-black. | Day and night is far more beautiful. |

## 2. The three-day clock

| When | Frames | Light |
|---|---|---|
| Day 1 dawn | Island 1 (PT-060 to 096, 114 to 122) | Cold blue pre-dawn, turning pale gold |
| Day 1 morning | Stage 1 (PT-123 to 134) | Clear fresh blue morning |
| Day 1 midday | Stage 2 (PT-135 to 144) | White-gold midday |
| Day 1 late afternoon | Stage 3, the Arena (PT-145 to 160) | Warm low golden light, then dusk and the **first campfire** (new frames) |
| Day 2 morning | Stage 4 (PT-161 to 177) | Clear morning, then midday and golden light on the Sleeping Giant |
| Day 2 afternoon and dusk | Stage 5, Flying (PT-178 to 188) | Golden light, then dusk, then the underside at night |
| Day 2 dusk and night | Stage 6, the Summit (PT-189 to 201) | Dusk, the Wraith, the night camp |
| Day 3 | The Throne (PT-202 to 220) | Pale dawn, then gold, then the Ring at dusk |

Every game frame prompt (PT-060 and later) now carries a **TIME OF DAY** line. The mind-vision frames (PT-097 to 113) have none: they are inside his head. If a frame has the wrong light, change only that line.

## 3. Where the 63 new frames go (insert points in the story)

| New frames | Group | Insert after |
|---|---|---|
| PT-221 to 223 | Day 1, Island 1: Pip wakes with him, the rock offers a bowl, the kettle on a warm stone | PT-122 |
| PT-224 to 230 | Day 1, Stages 1 and 2: the Pilfer Bird steals, the chase, Cloud Dumpling, three stones on a ledge, what the cairns say, the first glide, the wind that hates stillness | PT-144 |
| PT-231 to 236 | Day 1, Stage 3 evening: Glass Shadow copies his aim, sunset, first campfire alone, talking to the empty air, her whisper, the dormant Ring at night | PT-160 |
| PT-237 to 247 | Day 2, Stage 4: cold and hungry, Sour Cloud Berry, Gravel steps out, Stone Soup for two, Gravel carries him, Mirror Island, the Sleeping Giant, climbing it, it stirs, the Boot Bell, the Ember Pepper sneeze | PT-177 |
| PT-248 to 264 | Day 2, Stage 5: the false Throne, it melts, the string snaps, the rage arrow, the Eye weeps, "I'm sorry", the Eye tired, the Eye healthy, memory in the cloud, mending the string, the Quiet Island, bat-birds, falling through the floor, the underside world, the Sky Goose Egg, the Pilfer Bird returns, back up on a warm updraft | PT-188 |
| PT-265 to 271 | Day 2 night, Stage 6: a shadow too fast, the Wraith steps out, chased by himself, the kettle whistles, the Lantern Seed, night camp with Gravel, Gravel's gift | PT-201 |
| PT-272 to 283 | Day 3: the Staircase at dawn, Gravel holds the stair, Gravel becomes a cairn, the Wraith waits at the top, Elias stands still, the last step by breath, the fire lit by breath, the cairn stands up, "Mother, I'm still climbing", everyone together, the hidden door, credits sky | PT-202 and PT-220 |

They are listed at the end of the Playthrough page under groups that start with "Added", each saying where to insert it.

## 4. What reviewers will see (the first 30 minutes in order)

1. **0:00** Waking on a frosty ledge. A pebble rolls out of his pocket. The Eye is above.
2. **2:00** The living rock opens a bowl of soup. A small laugh.
3. **4:00** The Pilfer Bird steals his arrows. A chase.
4. **9:00** Three stones on a far ledge. Someone is watching.
5. **12:00** He steps off a ledge and his cloak catches the wind. **First "wow".**
6. **15:00** A wind that wants to push him off the moment he stands still.
7. **20:00** The Glass Shadow copies his aim. Dusk over the arena. His first fire, alone.
8. **25:00** He talks to a pebble. A warm light like a hand on his shoulder.

## 5. Build notes (for you)

- **New frame prompts are built like the old ones.** One image per prompt, the same locked costume, the same ring and rock rules, labels and header and footer. Attach: Elias reference, PT-002, and the creature sheet for Gravel, the bird or the Wraith.
- **Make the three creature sheets first** (CRE-11, 12, 13), then the frames that show them. Then PT-221 on.
- **Redo frames:** the Numbers-to-redo page is unchanged. The sky canon changed, so "dark sky" is no longer a fault in night and dusk frames; only storm-black or grey overcast is.
- **Production (Schreier):** the vertical slice is still **Island 1** (PT-060 to 122 plus PT-221 to 223). Build it grey-box first.

## 6. Bat-Birds are frightening (added after review)

The bat-birds are **CRE-14**: hawk-sized hunters with leathery bat wings, a hooked bird-skull head with a needle beak and small teeth, hot red-amber eyes and ash-grey skin. They hunt anything that stays still, so the player must run. The frame is **PT-259** (Bat-Birds Wake). They are not the soft Igara Birds (CRE-10).


## Canon: the Mother's age (added 16 Nov)
At nine Elias remembers a young Mother, about 32. At 21 she is 44, tired and thin, a few grey strands, never old. The parents of light appear as he remembers them from age nine. This wins over any earlier text that says the Mother is fifty or old.

# Props: use, HUD, sound and the pull to collect

> **Proposed.** Rule: every prop is used well, shown well on the HUD, sounds good, and is a joy to turn in the hand. Nothing in the pack is filler.

## The four tests every prop must pass
1. **A Moment.** One place where this prop is the answer, never a generic pickup.
2. **A Feel.** A signature sound family and a small haptic pulse.
3. **A Story.** One line of memory in the Hearth Shelf, for example the red thread Mother tied.
4. **A Show.** A silhouette you can tell at a glance and a model that is beautiful when it turns.

## HUD: no menu, no icons, real objects
- **Hip Ring.** Hold one button: a ring of the props he carries floats at his left hip. Each is the real 3D model, turning slowly (about 12 degrees per second). The selected one lifts, gets an ember rim light and hums its note. The world slows to about 20 percent, never a hard pause.
- **Shoulder Fan (arrows).** Arrow types fan over the shoulder. Each arrow shows its glowing tip and lights its neighbours. Stock is shown by the arrows physically in the quiver, never a number.
- **First Find Reveal.** The first time he gets any prop, the world dims, the prop floats to the camera and turns once with its sting, a one-word name appears, then it flies to its place on his body so the player learns where it lives. This happens once per prop.
- **Hearth Shelf.** At camp and on the Throne approach: a stone shelf of everything found. Grab and turn each with the mouse or stick, zoom to detail, read its one-line memory. Missing props show as a soft outline with a hint, so the gaps pull the player to explore.
- **Light follows the prop.** Ember props throw warm light on the room, cold props rim-light blue. A prop's own glow is its rotation light.
- **Condition is visible.** Torch burns down, kettle steams, gourd level shows through, quiver rattle gets hollow. No bars.

## Sound families
Bronze (tink, ring), Leather (creak, slap), Stone (tock, boom), Fire (whoomp, crackle), Air (breath, whoosh), Glass (chime, tink), Cloth (rustle, wrap), Water (slosh, pop), Living (chirp, heartbeat). Each prop is one family plus one signature note, always the same, so the player can name a prop with eyes closed. All arrow shots share one base pitch (the Sacred Arc's note) and add their own overtone.

## UE5 build notes
- Inspect view: SceneCapture2D render target on a UMG widget, real mesh, turntable plus drag rotate, per-prop rim-light colour.
- Prop Data Asset fields: Moment, Sound family, Signature note, Memory line, Rotation speed, Rim colour, Pickup Reveal Y/N.
- MetaSounds: one patch per family, parameterised by prop; quiver rattle driven by arrow count.
- Gamepad haptic: one short pulse on pickup, one on use, tuned per family.

## Every prop: what it does, fun ways to play, sound effects

### PRP-01 Sacred Arc
- **What it does:** Draws, aims and fires every arrow. Never burns itself. Its string hums one low note tuned to the Eye.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Pluck the string idle: it plays the note, and nearby lanterns answer with a glow.
  - Hold the draw longer and the inlay warms, then a held breath steadies the aim.
  - Tap the limb on stone: a hollow knock tells you if the rock behind is solid or hollow.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: deep wood groan. Draw: creak rising in pitch. Release: one low thrum. Idle: faint string hum. Fail: dry slack twang.

### PRP-02 Quiver
- **What it does:** Holds about two dozen ordinary arrows plus three sleeves for special arrows.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Flick a sleeve and the special arrow slides up to his hand.
  - Shake it (hold sprint, stop) to hear how many arrows are left.
  - Pip can sit on its rim and hand him an arrow.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: leather slap. Use: arrow slide and nock click. Idle: soft wood rattle, hollower as it empties. Fail: empty rattle and a sigh.

### PRP-03 Ordinary Arrow
- **What it does:** The everyday shot: switches, lanterns, Wraith stagger. Free and plentiful.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Shoot a bronze chime to ring a tune; match it to open the first door.
  - Shoot a hanging lantern chain to drop it for Pip to catch.
  - Stick three in a post and read them like a cairn: his path markers.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: wood clack. Use: clean thwip. Hit: wood thock on rock, bright ring on bronze. Fail: arrow skitters off stone.

### PRP-04 Fire Arrow
- **What it does:** Lights braziers and burns ash-webs. Needs a real flame to light and gutters in rain.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Light a line of braziers in one shot: a flame runs along the wick.
  - Hold it near Pip's pocket: his eyes glow with the firelight.
  - Wave it at a Wraith: it flinches and backs off.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: soft ember sizzle. Light: whoomp. Flight: crackle loop. Hit: flare and pop. Fail: hiss when wet.

### PRP-05 Rope Arrow
- **What it does:** Pins a cord to a far ledge so Elias can cross or climb it.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Pluck the cord like a string: the pitch tells you how tight it is.
  - Slide down it with a long zip and a whoop from Pip.
  - Tie off and swing across, letting go at the top of the swing.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: cord rustle. Fire: zing as cord pays out. Hit: tight twang. Climb: creak under weight. Fail: cord snaps loose.

### PRP-06 Chain Hook Arrow
- **What it does:** Hooks a hanging chain and swings a broken bridge into place.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Pull the chain and feel every link click through the controller.
  - Wind the chain around a post, then flick to ring it like a bell.
  - Swing a bridge so it knocks a loose stone to Gravel.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: iron clank. Fire: whoosh and rattle. Hook: heavy clang. Pull: ratchet clicks. Fail: chain slackens with a jingle.

### PRP-07 Lantern Arrow
- **What it does:** Lights far lantern anchors. Each one makes the Eye warm.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Shoot a far anchor and watch light run down the chain, anchor to anchor.
  - Aim near an anchor and the flame leans toward it.
  - Leave it in a dark corner as a small night-light for Pip.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: glass tink. Fire: breathy swell. Light: small bell when the anchor catches. Idle: candle flutter. Fail: flame gutters.

### PRP-08 Smoke Arrow
- **What it does:** Screens a crossing from Wraiths and hides his footsteps.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Pop it between two Wraiths so they bump heads.
  - Walk through the smoke: his steps go silent and the world muffles.
  - Smoke makes Pilfer sneeze and drop what he stole.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: clay clink. Pop: dull pop. Use: soft pfff. Idle: muffled world tone. Fail: thin puff.

### PRP-09 Echo Arrow
- **What it does:** Whistles into dark space. The returning echo draws the shape of a hidden room.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Whistle it down a long tunnel and hum back the pitch to find the exit.
  - Fire it into a cave: ripples of light trace the walls.
  - Flick the whistle holes with a thumb to play a little tune.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: bright tink. Fire: rising flute whistle. Echo: the whistle returns, bounced and softer. Fail: dead flat note.

### PRP-10 Stone Breaker Arrow
- **What it does:** Cracks fragile rock where an ember seam is trapped.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Hit a seam and the crack spreads like lightning.
  - Stack three in a row to blow a hole and hear the rumble roll.
  - Tap a wall first with a stone: the hollow ones answer.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: heavy thud. Fire: low whump. Hit: crack and boom. Rumble: rolling stone. Fail: dull clunk.

### PRP-11 Cinder Arrow
- **What it does:** Its crystal hum wakes Cinder seams and sends light running along them.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Hold the crystal to the Sacred Arc and the two notes harmonise.
  - Fire along a seam and the light runs like a lit fuse.
  - Put it in the dark: it hums softly like a nightlight.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: crystal chime. Fire: rising hum. Hit: orange ring. Idle: gentle harmonic hum. Fail: off-key buzz.

### PRP-12 Gust Arrow
- **What it does:** Pushes cloud bridges and spins vane wheels no hand can turn.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Fire it at a feather: it dances in the wind.
  - Blow a cloud bridge across, then walk it before it drifts.
  - Fire at a banner and read which way the wind is going.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: soft breath. Fire: whoosh with fluttering feathers. Hit: gust burst. Idle: faint breeze. Fail: limp flutter.

### PRP-13 Climbing Cord
- **What it does:** Lowers a villager or Pip down a cliff. A kindness tool as much as a climbing one.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Tie a knot with a quick two-button mini-game.
  - Lower Pip first and hear his tiny squeak as he drops.
  - Loop it around a rock and abseil with a whoosh.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: rope slap. Use: rope slide. Clip: carabiner snick. Fail: rope creak and a fray.

### PRP-14 Wedge Pitons
- **What it does:** Hammered in to make steps. Each tap is a different pitch.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Tap in order and the climb plays a rising scale.
  - Hammer with the stone hammer to the beat for a tight fit.
  - Leave a tune of pitons on a wall for other climbers.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: bronze jingle. Use: tink, rising one note per step. Fail: dull thud, slips.

### PRP-15 Flint and Steel
- **What it does:** Makes the first camp fire with Pip.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Strike in rhythm: faster means bigger sparks.
  - Light Pip's nose-glow for a joke: he sneezes embers.
  - Catch a spark in the cloth and blow it into a flame.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: leather flap. Strike: scrape and click. Spark: crackle. Fire: whoomp. Fail: dry click, no spark.

### PRP-16 Hand Lantern
- **What it does:** Lights dark passages with a soft amber that shows the Eye's memory glow.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Swing it and the shadows swing with it.
  - Set it on the ground: moths and sparks gather.
  - Cover the glass with his hand and the dark creeps in.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: ring creak. Use: chain jingle. Idle: candle flutter. Fail: flame gutters out with a sigh.

### PRP-17 Water Gourd
- **What it does:** Quenches Elias, cools an ember seam, calms a frightened companion.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Pour a little for Pip and he drinks with a squeak.
  - Splash an ember seam and watch it hiss to grey.
  - Tap it to hear how much is left.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: cork squeak. Open: pop. Drink: gulp. Pour: slosh. Empty: hollow tap. Fail: dry drip.

### PRP-18 Wrist Wraps
- **What it does:** Bound before every climb. The re-wrap at camp is a ritual of readiness.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Wrap in time with a small rhythm and the grip glows.
  - Pip tightens the last knot with his teeth.
  - Unwrap after a hard day to see the day's scrapes.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: cloth rustle. Wrap: winding swish. Buckle: snick. Fail: loose flap.

### PRP-19 Cairn Chalk
- **What it does:** Marks the route. Gravel recognises his marks and leaves a cairn beside them.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Draw an arrow on rock and Gravel answers with a stone.
  - Chalk your hand for a grippy climb.
  - Leave a small chalk smile for the next climber.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: dry clack. Use: chalk scratch. Cairn: stone clack. Fail: chalk crumbles.

### PRP-20 Ember Needle
- **What it does:** Points to the nearest thing not yet found. A kindness, not an objective marker.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Shake it and the needle spins, then settles with a chime.
  - Hold it out like a compass and it warms nearer treasure.
  - It shivers and points away when Wraiths are close.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: bronze ring. Use: spinning tick. Settle: bell chime. Wraith: nervous buzz. Fail: needle sticks with a click.

### PRP-21 Hand Torch
- **What it does:** Burns down in real time. Tunnels become a clock you can feel.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Light a second torch from the first to share the fire.
  - Wave it to scare away bats.
  - Poke the flame to make sparks, and Pip leaps.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: wood knock. Light: whomp. Use: crackle loop. Fail: sigh as it dies.

### PRP-22 Memory Shard
- **What it does:** Held to the light it plays a short memory film from the Eye.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Tilt it to move the picture like a window.
  - Hold to the Eye's light and the film plays larger.
  - Whisper to it in the dark and a different memory answers.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: warm glass chime. Use: room tone and a whisper fading in. Idle: soft hum. Fail: static fizz.

### PRP-23 Lantern Seed
- **What it does:** Planted at a dead lantern anchor where a bloom grows over a few breaths.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Warm it between his hands to crack it wider.
  - Plant it and wait: it grows as he waits.
  - Plant two in a row for a chain of blooms.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: seed crackle. Plant: soft thump. Bloom: chime. Idle: tiny pops. Fail: pod goes cold.

### PRP-24 Arrow Bundle
- **What it does:** The refill. Picking it up shows the twine untied and the arrows sliding into the quiver.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Untie the twine with two fingers.
  - Fan the arrows to choose a colour.
  - Pip steals one and Elias has to chase him.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: twine rustle. Open: wood clack. Slide: arrows into leather. Fail: twine snaps.

### PRP-25 Sky-Folk Relic
- **What it does:** Held to the ear it hums near Sky-folk marks and translates one carving.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Blow across the bone loop for a low whistle.
  - Hold it to a carving and the spirals glow.
  - Hum back and a hidden door answers.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: bone knock. Use: spiral hum. Near mark: breathy flute. Fail: flat silence.

### PRP-26 Still Secret
- **What it does:** Warm in the hand. Hold still and it glows gold.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Stop moving and the ring brightens.
  - Breathe with it: it pulses slow.
  - Place it on a cairn and everything goes quiet.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: soft tone. Use: a very slow heartbeat. Glow: a held, pure note. Fail: silence breaks.

### PRP-27 Cairn Gift
- **What it does:** Given by Gravel. Placed on his cairn it closes a friendship beat.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Rest it in his palm and feel it warm.
  - Stack a fourth pebble on top; Gravel grins.
  - Trade it for a tiny story.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: stone settle. Place: soft bell. Idle: warm hum. Fail: stones tumble.

### PRP-28 Mother Flatbread
- **What it does:** Eaten at a hard moment: a memory of Mother and a calm.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Tear in half and share with Pip.
  - Smell it: steam and a hummed lullaby.
  - Wrap again with the red thread.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: cloth unwrap. Tear: crisp rip. Eat: soft chew. Lullaby: two seconds hummed. Fail: crumbs fall.

### PRP-29 Wrist Thread
- **What it does:** A thumb-brush gives a heartbeat of Mother's memory when he is low.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Roll the bead between his fingers.
  - Tie and untie the knot when thinking.
  - Pip tugs it for attention.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: thread tug. Use: one bead click. Idle: a faint heartbeat. Fail: a frayed snap.

### PRP-30 Bronze Key
- **What it does:** Opens the one lock no arrow can.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Spin it on its ring.
  - Turn it in the lock: each pin clunks.
  - Pip tries to ride the ring.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: heavy chime. Turn: deep clunk. Door: slow groan. Fail: jam and rattle.

### PRP-31 Chirp Kettle
- **What it does:** Boiled at a camp it whistles a tune that matches Pilfer's call.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Whistle back and Pilfer answers.
  - Tap the dents like drums.
  - Pour tea for a frightened villager.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: copper clink. Boil: bubbling. Whistle: chirp tune. Fail: boil-dry crackle.

### PRP-32 Pocket Pebble Pip
- **What it does:** Pip in the pocket: his amber crack-eyes blink when a secret is near.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Rub him and he glows warmer.
  - Hold him up: he looks around.
  - Toss him gently and he lands with a tiny tick.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: tiny tick. Use: soft hum. Blink: faint glow tone. Fail: sleepy sigh.

### PRP-33 Boot Bell
- **What it does:** One dull ring on each step. Wrap in cloth to sneak.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Ring it to call Pip.
  - Stuff cloth in to sneak.
  - Kick it for a tune.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: bronze tink. Step: dull ring. Muffled: soft thud. Fail: clank.

### PRP-34 Cloud Dumpling
- **What it does:** Eaten before a long jump: extra hang time.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Squish it and it floats back.
  - Share half with Pip.
  - Float it up and catch it on a bow tip.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: pillowy squeak. Eat: soft puff. Jump: airy whoosh. Fail: deflates with a sigh.

### PRP-35 Ember Pepper
- **What it does:** Eaten in the cold: warmth and a small flame-breath.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Bite it: smoke curls from his ears.
  - Light a wick by breathing.
  - Pip sneezes sparks.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: crackle. Eat: sizzle. Breath: whomp. Fail: cough.

### PRP-36 Stone Soup
- **What it does:** Shared at camp. Gravel's friendship beat.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Stir and the stone turns.
  - Share a bowl with each friend.
  - Add a berry for tang.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: clay clunk. Stir: spoon tink. Eat: slurp. Fail: bubble stops.

### PRP-37 Sky Goose Egg
- **What it does:** Carried carefully to a nest. The goose that hatches carries Elias over a gap.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Hold it to his ear: tap tap inside.
  - Warm it in the nest of cloth.
  - Name the goose.
- **Sound effects:** Pickup: soft thump. Tap: shell tapping. Hatch: crack and chirp. Fail: a worried peep.

### PRP-38 Sour Cloud Berry
- **What it does:** Eaten for a laugh. A sour pucker, and Pip's reaction.
- **Fun ways to play:**
  - Squeeze one: it pops with a puff.
  - Feed Pip: he makes a face.
  - Share with Gravel: rock-face crumples.
