# The story in order: day, clock, what happens, narration, what they say

This is the Playthrough storyboard written out as a story, frame by frame, so anyone can follow it. It uses the three-day clock. **Day 1** runs from the cold pre-dawn on the Starting Shelf to the first night. **Day 2** is the hungry morning, Gravel, the Giant, the false Throne, the Eye weeping, the apology, the Wraith, the fall into the underside world and the second night. **Day 3** starts with the Eye healed, then the staircase, the last step by breath, the Throne, the Ring of Fire and the return of the people.

## The key answers

- **Where and when does he eat the soup?** Three times. Day 1, 07:30, dawn: the living rock opens a warm bowl (PT-222) at the end of Island 1, right after the shadow duel. Day 2, 07:50, morning: he shares Stone Soup with Gravel (PT-240). The cloud dumpling is Day 1 noon (PT-226).
- **Where does he get the Boot Bell?** From Gravel, Day 2 at 07:50, after the shared soup (PT-240): Gravel ties it on his boot so he can always find him. It jingles at the worst moment, at 16:17 in front of the Giant (PT-246).
- **When does the Giant come in?** Day 2, 15:20 (PT-181, PT-243). The climb is 16:00 to 17:30; it stirs at 16:15, the bell wakes the two Mage guards, he calms it, it becomes birds.
- **The cloud berry?** Day 2, 06:45, the first thing in the morning (PT-237, PT-238).
- **The Pilfer Bird and the "peep"?** It steals the Arrow Bundle Day 1 at 10:20 (PT-224), returns it Day 2 at 22:30 in the underside world (PT-263): a huge scary bird with a tiny squeaky voice, "peep". It sits on his shoulder once (PT-284).
- **The Eye weeping?** Day 2, 18:45, after the Rage Arrow (PT-252). He apologises at dusk (PT-253). The Eye is healed at Day 3 dawn (PT-255) and shows his memories.
- **The funny moments:** the kettle (PT-223, PT-268 where it beats the Wraith), the sour berry (PT-238), the Boot Bell (PT-246), the pepper sneeze (PT-247), the goose egg (PT-262), the "peep" (PT-263), Gravel asking for soup when he wakes (PT-279).


## Movie 1 · The Whole World (before)

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 1, THE WORLD, WHOLE):*

> NARRATOR: Once, there was a world that floated in the sky. It was whole, and it was bright, and it was home.
> NARRATOR: It was one great green island, drifting above a sea of cloud, with a mountain at its heart. Water gathered on the peak, fell in white ribbons from the cliffs, and turned to mist that rose again to meet the sky.
> NARRATOR: Our homes were carved into the rock itself, and when evening came, every round window glowed like a lantern. Ships shaped like sleeping rays came and went from the skyport. Birds crossed the sky in their thousands.
> NARRATOR: On the highest hill stood the Throne. And above it hung six lines of fire, one above the other, like a ladder up to the stars. They were always lit.
> NARRATOR: The Throne was the heart of our island. The fire rose up into the six lines, and flowed back down through the Throne into veins of gold that ran through all the rock. That fire held the stone together. It was what kept us in the sky. And like a breath, it rose and it fell.
> NARRATOR: Over all of it, the Eye watched, calm and open, made of the sky itself. And far away, in a slow and endless circle, the Dragon flew. It was never a danger to us. It was simply part of the world, the way the wind is.
> NARRATOR: In the morning, people walked the promenade in the pale light. Children chased the sparks that rose from the fire bowls. At night the musicians played, and the lanterns came on, one by one.
> NARRATOR: And at the heart of it all, my father kept the fire of the whole world.

### PT-001 Dawn Over Igara
**Long ago, before the break (a memory)**

- **What is happening:** Epic wide establishing shot at dawn, the fixed hero view from the south and slightly above, slow drift. The whole of Igara before the break at dawn, from the hero view, the island filling the middle of the picture. The Throne stands on the mountain with the six bars of fire above it. Skycraft glide in and out along the skyport trailing thin amber light, and a very few tiny people walk the skyport deck behind its rail.

- **Narrator:** "Six lines of fire hung in the sky, and they were always lit."

At his open forge the Father stands with his back to us at the great bronze fire bowl, hands in the flames, sparks pouring off his scarred hands and rising into the sky, the six lines in the distance answering him one by one. ## Movie 2 · The Family

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 2, A SMALL HOUSE, A GOOD LIFE):*

> NARRATOR: We lived in the rock, in a home with round windows.
> NARRATOR: My father was a big, warm man whose scarred hands glowed when he was happy. My mother was quiet. She always looked at the sky before she spoke.
> NARRATOR: One evening I ran in, and my father was juggling sparks in his bare hands, only to make me laugh. He tipped a few into my palms.
> FATHER (warm, playful): Harder, Elias! Put your whole heart into it!
> ELIAS, age 9 (small, honest): I did.
> FATHER (laughing): Then more heart!
> NARRATOR: The sparks fizzled in my hands. He laughed, and so did I. My mother watched from the window, a small smile on her face, her eyes on the sky.
> NARRATOR: My father could make fire dance. My mother could make it quiet. I was somewhere in between.
> NARRATOR: We ate by lamplight, the three of us. And while my father talked with his hands, I watched the flames in the hearth, and wondered what they were saying.

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 3, THE TURTLE):*

> NARRATOR: In the evenings, my mother told me the old story.
> MOTHER (soft, close): A young man once asked a wise old turtle, "What is it all about?" The turtle said nothing. It turned its back, and sat in the sun.
> NARRATOR: The young man grew angry, and walked away. Years later, he came back, and saw the pattern on the turtle's shell. And it was the answer.
> ELIAS, age 9 (curious): But why didn't the turtle just tell him?
> MOTHER (gentle, slow): Some things you can't be told, my love. You have to see them yourself.
> MOTHER: And when it goes dark, don't fight it. Don't run. Just wait. It comes back.
> NARRATOR: She touched my chest when she said it. I did not understand. Not yet.

## Movie 3 · The Quiet Season

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 4, THE QUIET SEASON):*

> NARRATOR: Then came the quiet season. No light. No spark. Just grey, and waiting.
> NARRATOR: One morning the fire simply did not come. The six lines flickered, and dimmed, and went grey. Nobody sang. People stood in their doorways, looking up, their arms folded. The lantern strings hung dark. It was not a disaster. It was only heavy, and flat, and very still.
> MOTHER (calm): Sit with me. It will pass.
> FATHER (pacing, pained): I can't just sit here. Look at them. Look at their faces.

## Movie 4 · The Push and the Break

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 5, THE PUSH):*

> NARRATOR: He climbed to the Throne alone. I ran after him, as far as the last bridge, and there I stopped. All I could see was his back, his hands, and his long shadow on the rock.
> ELIAS, age 9 (afraid): Father, don't!
> FATHER (not turning, loving, resolved): I'll bring the light back, son. I promise.
> NARRATOR: He raised both arms. He was not angry. He was doing it for everyone. And he did not give the Throne a little fire, the way you feed a flame. He gave it all of his, all at once.
> NARRATOR: He did it for love. That is the part that hurts.

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 6, THE BREAK):*

> NARRATOR: For one moment, the sky was glorious. Gold, everywhere, as far as I could see.
> NARRATOR: But it was too much. The Throne could not hold it. The fire poured down into the veins, and the veins blazed white through all the rock of the island, hills, cliffs and terraces, more fire than the stone could carry.
> NARRATOR: And then it cracked. A sound like a mountain splitting. The great island split along those glowing veins, and tore apart into pieces. Walkways snapped. People held on to what was left, and to each other.
> NARRATOR: The veins faded to dark. The six lines of fire went out, one by one, from the top down. The Eye closed. The Dragon swept through the falling rock and roared at the sky, but it could not stop it.
> NARRATOR: And my father was lost in the fire. I never saw him fall. The light just went out.
> ELIAS, age 9 (screaming, broken): FATHER!

- **Narrator:** Father: "I will bring the light back, son. I promise."

He is small and slight with short tousled dark-brown hair and wears a fitted high-collared tunic in soft grey-beige wool with a slim belt, slim trousers and soft dark boots; we see his back and the side of his face, his hands held open at his sides, his mouth open as he calls out.
- **Narrator:** Elias: "Father, don't!"

### PT-033 At the Throne
**The day of the break (a memory)**

The Father stands before the great Throne with both arms raised, a tiny figure against the colossal black monolith with six dark fissures. Wind whips his clothes. ### PT-034 The Father Feeds the Fire
**The day of the break (a memory)**

A huge column of white-gold light erupts from the Throne and fills the sky, the six lines blazing all at once brighter than ever, birds exploding upward, the whole world lit like noon. For one beat it is the most beautiful thing ever seen. At the same moment thin veins of gold light blaze through all the rock of the island below, running down from the Throne through the cliffs, hills and terraces like glowing roots, more and more of them, brighter than the stone can hold.

### PT-035 The Fire Wakes in Fright
**The day of the break (a memory)**

- **Where:** The past (movie)
- **What is happening:** Close dramatic shot on the Throne. The sleeping fire below wakes in fright: a black crack races up the face of the Throne monolith through the six fissures, white-gold light bursting out of it, stone shards exploding outward, and the gold veins in the rock of the whole island flare white-hot, the stone groaning and starting to split along them. The Father's silhouette is blown back by the light. Shock, speed, violence of light.

### PT-036 The Volcano Erupts
**The day of the break (a memory)**

- **Where:** The past (movie)

The crater at the foot of the Throne bursts open: a vast column of molten lava and black-orange ash erupts into the sky, the six lines swallowed in smoke, the Throne a black silhouette against the glare, lightning flickering inside the ash cloud. **The day of the break (a memory)**

## Movie 5 · The Leaving and the Years Away

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 7, THE LEAVING):*

> NARRATOR: Smoke. Silence. People ran for the last ships, with whatever they could carry.
> NARRATOR: My mother found me in the wreck of our home. She pressed something warm into my hands: a small, glowing ember. She folded my fingers closed around it.
> MOTHER (steady, tender): This is the last of my fire. Keep it. When you are lost, it will know the way. And Elias, listen: I will always be able to find you.
> NARRATOR: We left. I looked back. The Dragon did not follow. It circled the broken world, alone, while our ship grew smaller and smaller.
> NARRATOR: Everyone left. Everyone, except the dragon. It was part of the sky, and the sky was part of it.

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 8, THE YEARS AWAY):*

> NARRATOR: We lived in a grey city, in a tiny room, in the rain.
> NARRATOR: I grew. Nine. Thirteen. Seventeen. The teachers said, "Hurry up." The other boys said, "Try harder." I never did, and I never explained. I sat on the rooftops and watched the sky. The ember sat in a jar on the window, tiny and dim, nearly out. And my mother grew older.
> NARRATOR: Twelve years. I was told to hurry. I was told to try harder. But somewhere inside me, a small quiet voice kept saying: wait.
> NARRATOR: When I was twenty-one, I sat by her bed, and she took my hand.
> MOTHER, old (frail, whispering, loving): You were never slow, my love. You were listening. When it goes dark... wait. It comes back.
> NARRATOR: She closed her eyes. And she was gone.

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 9, THE CALL):*

> NARRATOR: Silence. Then, in my hand, the ember blazed, brighter than it had been in twelve years. A single line of fire drew itself across the night, pointing up.
> NARRATOR: I picked it up, and I walked out into the rain.
> NARRATOR: And so I went home. I did not know how to fix it. But something inside me knew the way.

## Day 1 · Island 1: waking, the beam, the Shadow

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 10, THE GAME BEGINS: THE STARTING SHELF):*

> NARRATOR: I opened my eyes on a bronze disc, floating in the dark, just before the dawn. Below me there was nothing but a sea of cloud.
> NARRATOR: I stood on the lowest island of the broken world. Cracked stone, a ravine, a fallen beam across it, and far ahead, a door.
> NARRATOR: I took my first steps. The Cinder drifted dimly beside me, like a small tired star.
> NARRATOR: Then I looked up. Island above island, tier above tier, climbing out of the cloud, and at the very top, small and far and dark, the Throne.
> NARRATOR: A shadow crossed the dawn, enormous, with slow wings. The Dragon. It did not look at me.
> NARRATOR: And at the far edge of the sky, low over the horizon, two faint lights hung side by side. I did not know what they were. I only knew I could not stop looking.

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 11, THE BEAM AND THE LOCKED DOOR):*

> NARRATOR: I walked to the rim. Old chains hung over the edge into the amber cloud, far below. I stepped back.
> NARRATOR: I crossed the beam slowly, one careful foot after the other, over the open drop.
> NARRATOR: When I ran, the world answered. Dust lifted. Stones skittered. A thin crack ran across the stone. The faster I moved, the louder everything got.
> NARRATOR: At the end of the road, a great door waited at the top of three broad steps, locked, with a heavy rusted chain. I pulled at it. Nothing. I pushed. Nothing.
> NARRATOR: So I stopped. I stood perfectly still. And the Cinder drifted to the padlock, and glowed, and the lock sprang open.
> NARRATOR: I could not explain how I knew. I only knew when I stopped.
> NARRATOR: Inside, in a quiet stone room, three weapons hung in the air, waiting. A bow wrapped in flame. A short bronze blade with a hot glowing edge. A long bronze lance. I reached out, and they came to me, and turned slowly around me like small moons.

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 12, THE SHADOW):*

> NARRATOR: As I stepped back into the light, my shadow fell across the stone. Too sharp. Too dark. And then it stood up.
> NARRATOR: It was a copy of me, made of dark amber glass, with no face. It stood in front of me, and it did exactly what I did. I drew a fire arrow. It drew one at the same instant, and the two arrows met in the air. I swung my blade. It swung its blade, and sparks sprayed where they locked. I thrust my lance. It thrust its own.
> NARRATOR: I struck harder. Faster. And the shadow split into three, and closed in around me.
> NARRATOR: A storm rose from nowhere. Dust and wind tore across the island, and the stone cracked at its edges. I staggered. A blow caught me, and threw me backward, and my weapons scattered in the air.
> NARRATOR: And then I did something I did not plan. I stopped. A thin bronze ring came down out of the light and hung above my head, perfectly still. The wind fell away.
> NARRATOR: I lowered my arms. The bow, the blade and the lance drifted from my hands, and hung in the air. I opened my empty hands.
> NARRATOR: The shadow tried to copy me. It could not. It flickered, and shimmered, and shook.
> NARRATOR: I closed my eyes. And I rose, a little, off the ground, and I was still.

## Day 1 · Inside his mind: the mind-movie

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 13, THE MIND-MOVIE):*

> NARRATOR: Behind my closed eyes, there was a plain as black as still water. On the far horizon, the six lines glowed faintly, like a sunrise.
> NARRATOR: A great storm of dust came charging at me, with lightning in its veins. A voice inside me said, run. Keep moving. I stayed. And it rushed straight through me, and was gone.
> NARRATOR: A knight made of fire stood in my way, and froze, and would not move, and the heaviness of it pressed on my chest. I did not push. I waited.
> NARRATOR: Small burning things crawled in at the edges of my mind, and bit, and would not go. They were only worries. I did not swat them. They fell away.
> NARRATOR: Glass shapes whispered, in my own voice, all the things I feared were true about me. I did not argue. I looked away, and they grew small.
> NARRATOR: And then the shadow and I fought, in the dark, at a size too big for the sky. Arrows. Blades. Sparks hanging in the air.
> NARRATOR: And then I stopped. I lowered everything. I stood open-handed in the middle of the world, and the sparks stood still around me.
> NARRATOR: Cracks ran across the shadow's face, and light poured out of them. It broke into a thousand pieces of amber glass, and they rose like dust toward the six lines. And the whole dark filled with gold.
> NARRATOR: I opened my eyes. The storm was gone. There was only a drift of amber dust, rising from the stone. And the great door stood open, lit, with a bridge beyond it, leading on.

## Day 1 · Island 1: waking up, breakfast from the world, the bridge

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 14, THE SECOND ISLAND):*

> NARRATOR: I crossed a bridge of planks and chains toward a second island, tall and twisted, like a tower leaning in the wind.
> NARRATOR: High above me, the Eye was shut, a vast dark shape in the sky. But in the very centre of it, I saw a single faint ember, like a pupil beginning to wake. And the lowest of the six lines pulsed, once, with the faintest amber light.
> NARRATOR: The wind was strong there, and the dust blew everywhere. But behind a ridge of dark rock, I found a pocket where the air was still. I stood in it, and my breathing slowed.
> NARRATOR: I threw the Cinder. It crossed the air like a streak of gold, and struck a small bronze lantern, and the lantern lit. A thread of light stretched from it back to my hand, and the Cinder came home.
> NARRATOR: I pressed it against a crust of black ore, hard as a shell. The shell cracked, and inside was an old chest. And when it opened, a soft light rose out of it, and in the air there hung a memory: a small window, in the evening, and a woman's voice telling an old story about a turtle.
> NARRATOR: I stopped. My shoulders dropped. And the Cinder came close to my cheek, warm and rose-gold. And I heard her.
> MOTHER (whisper): Slow down, my love.
> NARRATOR: A dark pillar of stone and bronze stood waiting at the island's edge. I held perfectly still in front of it, and the Cinder rose into its head, and the fire caught. And far above me, in the dark sky, the lowest line ignited. One line, burning steady and gold.

## Day 2 · Stage 4: hungry morning, Gravel, the Bridge of Leeches

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 17, STAGE FOUR: THE BRIDGE OF LEECHES):*

> NARRATOR: At the edge of a deep canyon between two sheer cliffs, I stood still, and a bridge of pure amber light formed in front of me.
> NARRATOR: Then, at the start of the chain bridge, I looked down, and saw them. Small, glossy, orange-glowing things, clinging to the chains and to the underside of every plank.
> NARRATOR: The whole bridge was alive. A carpet of them crawled along every plank, and every chain, and over every post. And under the bridge hung a forest of them, clusters of glowing sacs, dripping something dark.
> NARRATOR: I walked between them, stepping carefully around each one. More dropped onto me from above. They climbed my legs. They climbed my wrists. I could feel every tiny foot.
> NARRATOR: I drew the bow and fired along the rail, and a line of them burst into orange sparks. I stopped in the middle, and shook my whole body, and stamped, and they flew off in an arc. But there were always more. They always came back.
> NARRATOR: Then I stood still. And from my feet, thin rings of orange light spread across the bridge. And the leeches, wherever the rings touched them, let go, and slid away.
> NARRATOR: Once, I slipped. I fell backward through the dark cloud, and the Cinder streaked down after me, a ribbon of gold, and caught me.
> NARRATOR: In the middle of a fight, I stopped dead, and lowered my hands. A Burn Knight stood frozen behind me. And the Cinder came close, and I heard her.
> MOTHER (whisper): Breathe. I'm here.
> NARRATOR: Far beyond the canyon, the Dragon circled a broken tower of rock, breathing an arc of flame. And above me, four of the six lines blazed amber. The Eye was nearly open now, burning white and gold at its heart.

## Day 3 · The Throne, the Ring, the return and the end

*Chapter narration (existing script, chapter 20, THE THRONE):*

> NARRATOR: I turned, and I lowered myself into the deep stone seat. My hands came to rest on the thick armrests. I was small, in that great chair. And I did nothing. I did nothing at all.
> NARRATOR: The Cinder came to my chest, and dissolved, and its light flowed into the seams of my suit.
> NARRATOR: I raised my open hands. And from my cupped palms, a bird of gold-white fire lifted into the air, trailing thin threads of light.
> NARRATOR: This time the fire did not come in a flood. It rose slowly, the way it always had, one line at a time. The six fissures of the Throne ignited, from the bottom up, molten amber, each one brighter than the last. Then the whole Throne blazed. Every brazier on the stairs flared. Embers rose into the sky like a second dawn.
> NARRATOR: The Eye opened fully over the world, enormous and gold. Above it, all six lines burned. And far out at the edge of the world, a giant ring of fire lit, all the way around every island and every bridge.
> NARRATOR: Nothing exploded. The world just woke up.
> NARRATOR: The fire ran down through the Throne, into the veins in the rock, the same veins that had split us, and this time they filled with gold, and held. The broken islands slid back through the sky, toward each other. The snapped bridges knitted together with threads of gold. The cracks filled with light. And the pieces came together, into one great green island, whole again, floating.
> NARRATOR: The things I had fought became beautiful. The dust of the storms turned into flocks of birds. The glass shadows became tall windows of light. And the leeches became fireflies, drifting up from the grass.
> NARRATOR: All the great lanterns across the world, at every height, lit at once, steady and gold.
> NARRATOR: I sat against the blazing Throne, a small figure, at the top of the world. And above me, in the amber sky, two figures made of soft gold light appeared, a man and a woman, side by side. They were the two faint lights from the beginning. And they were looking down at me.
> FATHER, made of light (humble, warm): I'm sorry, son. I couldn't wait.
> ELIAS, age 21 (quiet, tearful, smiling): I know. It's all right, Father. I waited for you.
> MOTHER, made of light (hand on his shoulder): You listened. You heard it. It came back, my love.
> NARRATOR: They stayed a long moment. Then they faded, into the warm light.
> NARRATOR: Below, the ships came home. On the skyport, people stepped onto solid ground. An old woman knelt and touched the stone. Children ran. And that evening, the lanterns came on between the trees, and music rose from the balconies, and the festival returned.
> NARRATOR: The Eye closed slowly, in peace. The Dragon flew through the birds, as it always had. It never left. It was part of the world.
> NARRATOR: I never became a great fire-maker. I just learned to wait. And that boy... was me.

# Light, the Eye and the nights (the world is lit by its own fire)

**The rule.** The world is lit by its own Fire. The sun and the two moons exist, but the *life* of the light comes from the six sky lines and the Fire Eye. So the first day is DIM: no lines are lit and the Eye is shut, and the sun is only a pale smudge behind a smoky haze. Colours are muted. The only strong light comes from ember cracks, lanterns and the Cinder. Every line that ignites, and every time the Eye opens a little more, the whole world gets warmer and brighter. Night is not a switch either: it is the same world with the little light it has left. The player should feel the world healing in the colour of every scene.

**Day and night still happen (a three-day clock), but how bright a day is depends on the fire.** Day 1 is a dim day, Day 2 a clearer day, Day 3 a golden dawn. Night 1 is dark with three faint bars and a dull half-open Eye. Night 2 is the darkest night, because Elias hurt the Eye.

## Light ladder: what the world looks like, by sky lines lit

| Lines lit | Eye | Daytime look |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Shut and dark | The world is still dark and dim: colours muted and desaturated, soft low contrast, the sun only a pale smudge behind a thin smoky amber haze with almost no direct sunlight; the real light comes from ember cracks, lanterns and the Cinder. |
| 1 | Shut with one faint ember at its centre | The world is dim: a faint warmth returns to the haze, muted colours, the sun a soft pale disc, very soft shadows. |
| 2 | Slightly open, a dull amber slit | The world is hazy and soft: gentle warm light at medium-low brightness, colours slowly returning. |
| 3 | Half open and dull amber | The world is warm and readable: soft golden light at medium brightness. |
| 4 | Nearly fully open | The world is bright and warm: clear amber-gold light with long soft shadows. |
| 5 | Fully open and burning | The world glows: rich amber light from five bright lines. |
| 6 | Wide open, calm and healthy | The world is golden and radiant: six lines blaze, full warm glow. |

The Eye after PT-252 (it weeps): the lid closes, grey ash on the lid, the lines dim to embers. Night 2 and the Wraith and the underside all happen in this dimmed state. At Day 3 dawn the Eye is healthy again (PT-255).

## When each line lights, and what the Eye does

| Moment | Day, clock | Lines | Eye |
|---|---|---|---|
| Arrival, the Starting Shelf | Day 1, 05:30 | 0 | Shut and dark |
| Eye stirs (PT-121) | Day 1, 08:12 | 0 | A faint ember wakes in it |
| Line 1 ignites (PT-134) | Day 1, 11:15 | 1 | Shut, ember growing |
| Line 2 ignites (PT-144) | Day 1, 13:50 | 2 | Slightly open |
| Eye half open (PT-158) | Day 1, 17:09 | 2 | Half open |
| Line 3 ignites (PT-160) | Day 1, 17:30 | 3 | Half open, dull amber |
| Night 1 | Day 1, 20:30 to 06:30 | 3 (faint) | Half-lidded, like a dull lamp |
| Line 4 ignites (PT-177) | Day 2, 13:30 | 4 | Nearly fully open |
| Line 5 ignites (PT-185, the Giant becomes birds) | Day 2, 17:15 | 5 | Fully open and burning |
| The Rage Arrow and the Eye weeps (PT-251, 252) | Day 2, 18:45 | 5, dimming to embers | Closing, a tear of fire |
| Night 2 | Day 2, 21:00 to Day 3, 05:50 | 5 (embers) | Half closed, grey ash |
| The Eye heals (PT-255) | Day 3, 06:10 | 5, burning bright again | Wide open and healthy |
| Line 6 ignites (PT-195) | Day 3, 07:19 | 6 | Wide open |
| Sits on the Throne, the Ring ignites (PT-208) | Day 3, 08:16 | 6 + the Ring | Open, blazing |

## The nights, one by one

### The night before the game: the arrival (PT-061, PT-221)
- **Where he sleeps:** on the bronze arrival disc as it carries him up out of the grey world in the dark, curled with his cape over him.
- **Who is with him:** nobody. Pip is in his cape pocket, the Cinder beside him, dim.
- **Light:** none from the sky. The disc has a faint bronze edge-glow, the Cinder a small rose-gold spark.
- **Sounds:** the disc's low hum, thin wind, cloth moving, nothing else.
- **What happens:** at 05:30 he wakes in cold blue pre-dawn with frost on his cape, and Pip opens its eyes.

### Night 1: the first night (Day 1, 20:30 to Day 2, 06:30; PT-232 to PT-236, PT-237)
- **Where he sleeps:** in a shallow rock hollow on the arena island's edge. The cracks in the rock glow warm and give a little heat. He lies curled on his cape on warm stone, scarf as a pillow, the bow within reach.
- **Who is with him:** nobody. Pip sleeps in his palm and the Cinder floats dim by his head. He talks to the empty space beside him (PT-234). His mother's whisper comes as warm light on his shoulder, never a person (PT-235).
- **What he does first:** at dusk he sits tiny at the arena's edge (PT-232). He eats a hot Ember Pepper by a small fire (PT-233), alone.
- **Light sources:** the small fire, the glowing cracks, lanterns on the chains, three faint sky bars, the half-open Eye as a dull amber lamp, two moons, thin stars through haze, the dormant ring as a thin dark ember line far out.
- **Sounds:** fire crackle, rock ticking as it cools, chains clinking softly in the wind, a lantern wick hiss, Pip's tiny clicks, his slow breathing, one very far low Dragon call. No music except a faint warm hum for the whisper.
- **Safe or not:** safe. The world is still, the stage is over. The danger is loneliness.
- **Morning:** he wakes to frost and a loud stomach growl (PT-237) at 06:30 under three faint bars, and the cloud berry bush leans down.

### Night 2: the second night (Day 2, 21:00 to Day 3, 05:50; PT-259 to PT-271)
- **How he gets there:** he apologises to the Eye (PT-253), walks alone through the silence (PT-258), is chased by the Wraith and saved by the kettle (PT-265 to PT-268). The Bat-Birds wake as the last light goes, the floor breaks and he falls (PT-259, PT-260) into the underside world (PT-261).
- **Where he sleeps:** in a cradle of two thick roots lined with soft glowing moss in the underside forest, under the island. The forest hangs upside down with its own light.
- **Who is with him:** Gravel arrives, rolling down through the cloud. Rock does not sleep: he sits upright beside Elias humming low, a hand on the root, stacking a little cairn (PT-270). The Pilfer Bird roosts on a root above with one eye open, and makes tiny "peep" noises in its sleep (PT-263, PT-284). Pip sleeps in his palm. The Lantern Seed glows inside his coat (PT-269). The goose with the egg honks once somewhere far (PT-262).
- **Light sources:** pale blue-green moss, amber fungus lanterns, the Lantern Seed, a small fire at the open edge, two moons and thin stars through gaps in the roots. The sky above is dark and the Eye is dull and half closed (it wept). The five lines are only faint embers. This night is darker than Night 1 even though more lines are lit, because he hurt the Eye. That is the point of the scene.
- **Sounds:** water trickling upward, soft glass-chimes from the fungus, dripping, a low hum, fire crackle, stones clicking as Gravel stacks, Gravel's low grinding hum like a lullaby, the bird's sleepy peeps, Pip's clicks, his breath.
- **What happens:** he mends the bow string with the Wrist Thread while Gravel holds the bow (PT-257). Gravel gives him the cairn gift: a flat stone with a carved spiral and a tiny flower, THANK YOU (PT-271). He lies down.
- **Safe or not:** safe, because everyone here is a friend. The cold comes only from what he did.
- **Morning:** at 05:50 a warm golden updraft lifts him out with the bird beside him (PT-264). The Eye opens wide and healthy at 06:10 (PT-255).

### Day 3: dawn, not another night
Day 3 ends at the Throne at about 09:30 in golden morning. There is no third night in the game.

## Sound by light level (ambience that grows as the world heals)
- **Dim day (0 to 1 lines):** thin wind, creaking chains, the Cinder's whistle, almost no birds. The silence is the sound.
- **Hazy day (2 lines):** a few distant bird calls return, chains clank, the first warm hum from the sky lines.
- **Warm day (3 to 4 lines):** more birds, wind chimes in the lanterns, distant Dragon calls, running water.
- **Bright day (5 lines):** full birdsong, a steady low note from the Eye, rushing wind.
- **Throne (6 lines and the Ring):** a full choral chord under everything, bells, the Dragon's low purr.
- **Night:** fire, cooling rock, chains, wind, one Dragon call. Never total silence unless the story needs it (PT-258, the Quiet Island).

## UE5 build notes
- One master variable, **FireLevel (0 to 6)**, drives sky colour, sun intensity, fog colour, exposure, ambient audio mix and lantern brightness. A second variable, **EyeState** (shut, stirring, half, open, wept, healthy), drives the Eye mesh and a soft sky-glow light.
- Day and night come from a separate **ClockTime** (Day 1 05:30 to Day 3 09:30). Night 2 applies a **Dimmed** multiplier to the lines after the Eye weeps.
- The underside forest uses its own light set: glowing moss, fungus lantern point lights, the Lantern Seed as a small warm light that follows Elias.
